exercises.name: Flat Bench Press
steps: Lie flat on the bench.
Grip just wider than shoulder width.
Lower the bar under control to your mid-chest.
Press up in a straight line without flaring your elbows to 90°+.
Keep your shoulder blades pinned back and feet flat on the floor the whole rep.

exercises.name: Incline Bench Press
steps: Same bar path as a flat press but on a 30–45° incline bench.
Lower to your upper chest/collarbone, not your neck, and avoid arching your lower back to make up the range of motion.

exercises.name: Decline Bench Press
steps: On a decline bench with your feet locked.
Lower the bar to your lower chest and press straight up.
Keep the motion controlled since the decline angle makes it easy to bounce the bar off your chest.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Bench Press
steps: Press two dumbbells from chest level to lockout.
Letting your wrists stay stacked over your elbows.
The extra stabilization demand means going lighter than your barbell press is normal and safer.

exercises.name: Incline Dumbbell Press
steps: Dumbbell press on an incline bench.
Pressing up and slightly inward.
Control the lowering phase, since dumbbells let your shoulders drift into a riskier position if you rush the eccentric.

exercises.name: Decline Dumbbell Press
steps: Dumbbell press on a decline bench.
Targets the lower chest more than a flat or incline press; press up and slightly in rather than straight up, and control the dumbbells down to full stretch each rep.

exercises.name: Floor Press
steps: Dumbbell press lying flat on the floor instead of a bench.
Your upper arms stop against the floor at the bottom of each rep, which naturally caps the range of motion and keeps your shoulders out of the deepest, riskiest position.

exercises.name: Chest Fly
steps: With a slight bend in your elbows held constant.
Lower the dumbbells out to the sides in a wide arc until you feel a stretch across your chest.
Squeeze them back together.
This is a stretch/isolation move, not a pressing move, so keep the load moderate.

exercises.name: Cable Crossover
steps: Standing between two cable stacks.
Pull both handles down and across your body in an arc, finishing with your hands crossing in front of your hips.
Keep a slight forward lean and soft elbows throughout.

exercises.name: Pec Deck
steps: Seated on the machine with your back flat against the pad.
Bring the arms together in front of your chest without letting your shoulders roll forward.
A controlled, machine-guided version of a chest fly.

exercises.name: Push-Up
steps: Hands slightly wider than shoulders, body in a straight line from head to heels.
Lower your chest to just above the floor, elbows at roughly 45° from your torso.
Push back up without letting your hips sag.

exercises.name: Incline Push-Up
steps: Hands on a bench, box, or step, body straight from head to heels.
The elevated hand position makes this an easier push-up variation, biased slightly toward the lower chest, good for building up to a standard push-up.

exercises.name: Decline Push-Up
steps: Feet elevated on a bench or step, hands on the floor, body straight from head to heels.
The elevated foot position makes this a harder push-up variation, biased slightly toward the upper chest and shoulders.

exercises.name: Dips
steps: On parallel bars.
Lower your body until your shoulders drop just below your elbows, leaning forward slightly to bias the chest.
Going deeper than that adds shoulder strain without adding much benefit.

exercises.name: Landmine Press
steps: With one end of a barbell anchored in a landmine sleeve.
Press the other end up and slightly forward from shoulder height.
The fixed arc is easier on the shoulder joint than a straight overhead press.

exercises.name: Resistance Band Chest Press
steps: Anchor a band behind you at chest height and press both handles forward until your arms are extended.
Control the return.
Keep tension on the band the whole rep instead of letting it go slack at the back.

exercises.name: Smith Machine Bench Press
steps: Press the fixed bar straight up and down on a Smith machine.
The guided track lets you push closer to failure without a spotter, so control the descent to your mid-chest and don't bounce.

exercises.name: Smith Machine Incline Press
steps: Same guided press on a 30–45° incline bench.
Lower to your upper chest and drive up.
Letting the fixed track take the balancing work so you can focus on the squeeze.

exercises.name: Machine Chest Press
steps: Sit with the handles at mid-chest height and press straight out until your arms are nearly locked.
Return under control.
A beginner-friendly way to overload the chest with no balance demand.

exercises.name: Incline Machine Chest Press
steps: A seated machine press angled to bias the upper chest.
Press up and slightly in, and stop just short of lockout to keep constant tension on the pecs.

exercises.name: Hammer Strength Chest Press
steps: A plate-loaded converging press where the handles arc toward each other at the top for a stronger peak contraction.
Press evenly with both arms and control the stretch.

exercises.name: Wide-Grip Bench Press
steps: A barbell bench with a grip wider than shoulder width to bias the chest over the triceps.
Shorten the range slightly and keep your shoulder blades pinned to protect the shoulders.

exercises.name: Reverse-Grip Bench Press
steps: Bench with an underhand (supinated) grip to shift load onto the upper chest.
Use a spotter.
Keep the wrists stacked, and start lighter since the grip feels unfamiliar.

exercises.name: Spoto Press
steps: A bench press paused an inch off the chest rather than touching.
The mid-air hold kills momentum and builds pressing strength off the bottom; hold for a beat.
Drive up.

exercises.name: Board Press
steps: A partial bench press to a board (or foam block) on the chest, training lockout strength through a shortened range.
Press explosively off the board without bouncing.

exercises.name: Pin Press
steps: A bench press starting from dead-stop on the rack's safety pins, removing the stretch reflex.
Press from a full stop to build raw power out of the bottom position.

exercises.name: Neutral-Grip Dumbbell Press
steps: Press two dumbbells with palms facing each other.
The neutral grip is easier on the shoulders and hits the inner chest and triceps hard; keep the dumbbells stacked over the elbows.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Squeeze Press
steps: Press two dumbbells while actively pushing them together the whole rep.
The constant inward pressure maximizes chest activation; use a lighter load and feel the pecs squeeze at the top.

exercises.name: Svend Press
steps: Press a single weight plate (or two pressed together) straight out from your chest with both palms, crushing it inward the whole time.
A pure inner-chest contraction move with light load.

exercises.name: Incline Dumbbell Fly
steps: On an incline bench, open two dumbbells in a wide arc with a slight elbow bend, feeling the upper-chest stretch.
Hug them back together.
Keep the elbows soft and never lock them.

exercises.name: Decline Dumbbell Fly
steps: On a decline bench, arc two dumbbells out and back with a soft elbow bend to bias the lower chest.
Control the stretch and squeeze the pecs at the top.

exercises.name: Flat Dumbbell Fly
steps: Lying flat, open two dumbbells in a wide arc with slightly bent elbows until you feel a chest stretch.
Bring them together over your chest.
Think 'hugging a barrel,' not pressing.

exercises.name: Incline Cable Fly
steps: Set the cables low and fly upward and inward on an incline bench (or standing) to load the upper chest with constant tension.
Squeeze the pecs together at the top of each rep.

exercises.name: Low-to-High Cable Fly
steps: From low pulleys.
Sweep both handles up and together toward eye level, biasing the upper chest.
Keep a soft elbow bend and finish with the hands crossing or touching.

exercises.name: High-to-Low Cable Fly
steps: From high pulleys.
Sweep both handles down and together toward your hips to bias the lower chest.
Squeeze at the bottom and resist the stretch on the way back up.

exercises.name: Single-Arm Cable Fly
steps: A one-arm cable fly across the body.
The single-side setup lets each pec work through a fuller range and evens out strength differences; control the stretch behind you.

exercises.name: Resistance Band Fly
steps: Anchor a band behind you and fly both handles together in front of your chest.
The band's tension peaks at full contraction, so pause and squeeze the pecs at the finish.

exercises.name: Machine Fly
steps: Seated pec-deck-style fly with arms on the pads or handles.
Bring the arms together in a smooth arc and squeeze.
Keeping the shoulders down and back throughout.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Pullover
steps: Lying across or along a bench.
Lower one dumbbell in an arc behind your head with slightly bent arms, feeling the chest and lat stretch.
Pull it back over your chest.

exercises.name: Cable Pullover
steps: Standing at a high pulley with a rope or bar.
Keep your arms long and pull the handle down in an arc to your thighs.
A constant-tension pullover for the chest and lats.

exercises.name: Wide-Grip Push-Up
steps: A push-up with hands well outside shoulder width to emphasize the chest.
Keep a straight line from head to heels and lower until your chest nearly touches the floor.

exercises.name: Close-Grip Push-Up
steps: A push-up with hands close together under your chest to shift load onto the triceps and inner chest.
Keep the elbows tucked toward your sides as you lower.

exercises.name: Archer Push-Up
steps: A push-up shifting your weight over one arm while the other stays straight out to the side.
A bodyweight step toward the one-arm push-up; alternate sides each rep.

exercises.name: Deficit Push-Up
steps: A push-up with hands raised on blocks or plates so your chest sinks below hand level.
The extra range deepens the chest stretch; control the bottom and don't sag your hips.

exercises.name: Weighted Push-Up
steps: A standard push-up with a plate or weighted vest on your back to add resistance once bodyweight reps get easy.
Keep the core braced so the load doesn't sink your hips.

exercises.name: Ring Push-Up
steps: A push-up on gymnastic rings.
The unstable handles force the chest and stabilizers to work overtime; keep the rings from flaring and turn the palms out at the top to squeeze.

exercises.name: Clap Push-Up
steps: An explosive push-up where you push hard enough to leave the floor and clap before landing softly.
A power move for the chest; reset your line before each rep.

exercises.name: Feet-Elevated Push-Up
steps: A push-up with your feet raised on a bench or box to shift more load to the upper chest and shoulders.
Keep a rigid plank line and lower with control.

exercises.name: Weighted Chest Dip
steps: A chest dip with a belt or dumbbell for added load.
Lean your torso forward and let the elbows flare slightly to bias the chest; lower until you feel the stretch.
Press up.

exercises.name: Ring Dip
steps: A dip on rings.
Adding a big stability demand over parallel bars.
Keep the rings tight to your body.
Lean forward for chest.
Press to a strong lockout with the palms turned out.

exercises.name: Machine-Assisted Dip
steps: A dip on an assisted machine that supports part of your weight via a knee pad.
Lets you build to full bodyweight dips with clean depth and a forward chest lean.

exercises.name: Standing Cable Chest Press
steps: From chest-height pulleys.
Press both handles forward and together while standing.
The core braces against the load, making it a chest press plus anti-rotation trainer.

exercises.name: Single-Arm Machine Chest Press
steps: A one-arm chest press on a machine.
Pressing one side at a time adds an anti-rotation core demand and lets you even out left/right strength; control the return.

exercises.name: Guillotine Press
steps: A wide-grip bench press lowered toward the neck/upper chest with elbows flared to maximize chest stretch.
A shoulder-demanding variation, so go light and use a spotter.

exercises.name: Larsen Press
steps: A bench press with your legs held straight out (no leg drive or foot contact).
It removes the arch and forces the chest and shoulders to do all the work; keep it strict and lighter.

exercises.name: Incline Cable Press
steps: An incline press using cables instead of a bar, giving smooth constant tension up the whole range.
Press up and slightly together, and stop short of lockout to keep the pecs loaded.

exercises.name: Plate Pinch Press
steps: Press a weight plate held between flat palms out and back from your chest, crushing it the entire time.
Combines an inner-chest squeeze with a grip challenge; keep it light and slow.

exercises.name: Banded Push-Up
steps: A push-up with a resistance band looped across your upper back and held under both hands.
The band adds tension that peaks at lockout, overloading the top of the press.

exercises.name: Incline Dumbbell Squeeze Press
steps: An incline dumbbell press keeping the weights pressed together the whole rep.
The constant inward pressure lights up the upper and inner chest; go lighter and squeeze at the top.

exercises.name: Paused Bench Press
steps: A barbell bench press held motionless on the chest for a full second before pressing.
Killing the stretch reflex builds raw strength off the bottom; stay tight through the pause.

exercises.name: Feet-Up Bench Press
steps: A bench press with the feet lifted onto the bench instead of planted.
Removing leg drive forces the chest and shoulders to do all the work and teaches a properly braced torso.

exercises.name: Neutral-Grip Dumbbell Bench Press
steps: A dumbbell bench press with the palms facing each other throughout.
The neutral grip is much kinder to cranky shoulders while still loading the chest and triceps hard.

exercises.name: Single-Arm Dumbbell Bench Press
steps: A dumbbell bench press done one arm at a time.
The offset load turns it into a serious anti-rotation core exercise too; keep the hips square to the bench.

exercises.name: Close-Grip Incline Bench Press
steps: An incline barbell press with the hands about shoulder-width apart.
Shifts load onto the upper chest and triceps; keep the elbows tucked and press toward the collarbone.

exercises.name: Guillotine Bench Press
steps: A flared-elbow bench press lowered toward the neck rather than the sternum, biasing the upper chest.
Go light, use a spotter, and never let the bar drop.

exercises.name: Parallel Bar Dip
steps: A bodyweight dip on parallel bars, lowering until the upper arms are roughly parallel to the floor.
The baseline dip; keep the shoulders down and press back to a soft lockout.

exercises.name: Straight-Bar Dip
steps: A dip on a single straight bar, which forces the body to lean back over the bar.
Harder on the shoulders and much more of a chest and core challenge; build up slowly.

exercises.name: Banded Dip
steps: A dip with a resistance band looped under the knees to take some bodyweight off.
The best way to own the full range while you build toward unassisted reps.

exercises.name: Weighted Ring Dip
steps: A ring dip with a dip belt or weight vest added.
Ring instability plus real external load is about as hard as pressing gets; keep the rings pinned to your sides.

exercises.name: Feet-Elevated Bench Dip
steps: A bench dip with the heels up on a second bench or chair.
Elevating the feet loads the triceps much harder than the floor version; keep the hips close to the bench.

exercises.name: Slow-Negative Dip
steps: A dip lowered over three to five seconds, then reset by stepping or jumping back to the top.
Eccentric-only work builds the strength for full reps faster than assisted ones.

exercises.name: Chest-Lean Dip
steps: A dip with a deliberate forward torso lean and flared elbows to bias the chest over the triceps.
Let the chest travel toward the hands and stop when the shoulders feel the stretch.

exercises.name: Upright Dip (Tricep Focus)
steps: A dip kept as vertical as possible with the elbows tucked to your sides.
The upright torso hands the work to the triceps; a great heavy tricep builder.

exercises.name: Dip Support Hold
steps: Hold the top of a dip with locked arms and the shoulders pushed down away from the ears.
Builds the shoulder stability and lockout strength dips need before you chase reps.

exercises.name: Barbell Pullover
steps: Lying on a bench, lower a barbell back over your head with slightly bent arms, then pull it back over the chest.
Stretches and loads the chest and lats; keep the ribs down.

exercises.name: Machine Pullover
steps: A seated pullover machine that arcs the arms from overhead down to the torso.
Constant tension on the lats with no balance demand; squeeze at the bottom and control the return.

exercises.name: EZ-Bar Pullover
steps: A pullover with an EZ-bar, whose angled grips take strain off the wrists.
Keep a soft elbow bend and move only at the shoulders.

exercises.name: Cross-Bench Dumbbell Pullover
steps: A dumbbell pullover lying across a bench rather than along it, so the hips can drop for a deeper stretch.
A classic ribcage and lat builder; go light and controlled.

exercises.name: Incline Dumbbell Pullover
steps: A dumbbell pullover on a 30-45 degree incline bench.
The angle keeps tension on the lats and chest right through the top of the arc.

exercises.name: Single-Arm Cable Pullover
steps: A straight-arm cable pullover done one side at a time from a high pulley.
Lets each lat work through its own full range; keep the torso still and the arm long.

exercises.name: Kettlebell Pullover
steps: A floor or bench pullover holding a kettlebell by the horns.
The offset weight makes the stretched position feel heavier; brace so the low back doesn't arch.

exercises.name: Resistance Band Pullover
steps: A pullover against a band anchored behind your head while lying on the floor.
Band tension peaks at the top of the arc, making it a joint-friendly lat and chest option at home.

exercises.name: Rope Cable Pullover
steps: A standing straight-arm pullover with a rope on a high pulley, pulling down and past the hips.
Splitting the rope at the bottom gives a stronger lat squeeze.

exercises.name: Wide-Grip Lat Pulldown
steps: Grip the bar wider than shoulder width.
Lean back slightly.
Pull it down to your upper chest by driving your elbows down and back.
Avoid using body momentum to yank the weight down.

exercises.name: Close-Grip Lat Pulldown
steps: Same pulldown motion with a narrow, often V-handle grip.
Pull to your upper chest.
Squeezing your shoulder blades together at the bottom before controlling the weight back up.

exercises.name: Straight-Arm Pulldown
steps: Keeping your arms almost fully straight.
Pull the bar down from overhead to your thighs using your lats, not your arms.
Think of hinging at the shoulder only, like closing a stiff door.

exercises.name: Pull-Up
steps: From a dead hang with an overhand grip.
Pull your chin above the bar by driving your elbows down toward your hips.
Avoid kipping/swinging if the goal is strict back strength.

exercises.name: Chin-Up
steps: Same movement as a pull-up but with an underhand grip, which shifts more work onto your biceps.
Pull your chest toward the bar rather than just your chin.

exercises.name: Bent-Over Row
steps: Hinge forward from the hips with a flat back until your torso is roughly 45°.
Row the bar to your lower ribs.
Driving your elbows straight back.
Avoid standing up mid-rep to cheat the weight.

exercises.name: Seated Cable Row
steps: Sit with a slight forward lean.
Pull the handle to your abdomen while driving your chest up and squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Keep your torso still rather than rocking to add momentum.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Row
steps: With one knee and hand on a bench for support.
Row the dumbbell straight up toward your hip.
Keeping your torso parallel to the floor and avoiding any twisting at the top.

exercises.name: Single-Arm Dumbbell Row
steps: Same setup as a dumbbell row.
Focusing on one side at a time so you can feel and correct any imbalance between your left and right back strength.

exercises.name: T-Bar Row
steps: Straddling the bar with a chest-supported or free-standing hinge.
Row the handle up to your torso.
Keep your lower back braced and avoid jerking the weight up with momentum.

exercises.name: Inverted Row
steps: Lying under a bar set at hip height.
Pull your chest to the bar while keeping your body in a straight plank line.
Adjust difficulty by raising or lowering the bar height.

exercises.name: Resistance Band Row
steps: Anchor a band in front of you at chest height.
Row the handles to your ribs by driving your elbows straight back.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the end instead of just bending your elbows.

exercises.name: Renegade Row
steps: From a push-up plank position with a dumbbell in each hand.
Row one dumbbell up to your hip while bracing hard through your core to keep your hips from rotating.
Alternate sides each rep.

exercises.name: Deadlift
steps: Feet hip-width, bar over mid-foot, flat back.
Push the floor away with your legs while keeping the bar close to your shins as it rises, locking out with your hips, not your lower back.

exercises.name: Sumo Deadlift
steps: A wide stance with toes turned out.
Gripping inside your knees.
The more upright torso reduces lower-back strain compared to a conventional deadlift.
Keep your knees tracking over your toes throughout.

exercises.name: Rack Pull
steps: A partial deadlift starting from pins set around knee height.
Focuses on the lockout portion of the pull, so keep the same braced, flat-back technique even though the range of motion is shorter.

exercises.name: Romanian Deadlift (RDL)
steps: Starting from standing.
Push your hips straight back while keeping a slight knee bend and the bar close to your legs.
Lowering until you feel a deep hamstring stretch.
Drive your hips forward to stand back up.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Romanian Deadlift
steps: Same hip-hinge pattern as a barbell RDL but with a dumbbell in each hand.
Push your hips back until you feel a stretch in your hamstrings.
Keeping the dumbbells close to your legs the whole way down.

exercises.name: Stiff-Leg Deadlift (SLDL)
steps: Similar to an RDL but with straighter (not locked) knees.
Isolating the hamstrings more directly.
Stop lowering the bar once your lower back starts to round.

exercises.name: Good Morning
steps: With a bar across your upper back.
Hinge forward from the hips like a bow.
Keeping your back flat, until your torso is near-parallel to the floor.
Reverse the motion.
Use light weight until your hip-hinge is dialed in.

exercises.name: Neutral-Grip Lat Pulldown
steps: A lat pulldown using a neutral (palms-facing) V-handle.
Easier on the shoulders and biceps-friendly; pull the handle to your upper chest and drive the elbows down and back.

exercises.name: Reverse-Grip Lat Pulldown
steps: A pulldown with a shoulder-width underhand grip to bias the lower lats and hit the biceps more.
Pull the bar to your chest.
Leading with the elbows.
Squeeze at the bottom.

exercises.name: Single-Arm Lat Pulldown
steps: A one-arm cable pulldown that lets each lat move through a fuller range and evens out imbalances.
Pull the handle down and slightly back.
Rotating the torso for extra stretch.

exercises.name: Machine Lat Pulldown
steps: A plate-loaded or selectorized pulldown machine with a chest pad.
The fixed path lets you focus purely on driving the elbows down to your sides and squeezing the lats.

exercises.name: Kneeling Cable Pulldown
steps: Kneel facing a high pulley and pull a rope or bar down to your collarbone.
The kneeling position removes leg drive and isolates the lats through a strict vertical pull.

exercises.name: Wide-Grip Pull-Up
steps: A pull-up with hands well outside shoulder width to emphasize the lats and upper back.
Pull your chest toward the bar and avoid swinging; add weight once strict reps are easy.

exercises.name: Neutral-Grip Pull-Up
steps: A pull-up on parallel (palms-facing) handles.
The most shoulder-friendly grip, blending lat and mid-back work; pull to chest height and control the descent.

exercises.name: Commando Pull-Up
steps: A pull-up gripping the bar lengthwise with hands together, pulling your head to one side then the other.
Hits the lats and arms with an added rotational challenge.

exercises.name: Weighted Pull-Up
steps: A strict pull-up with a dip belt or dumbbell between the feet for added load.
Keep every rep full-range from a dead hang to chin over the bar; ideal for building back strength.

exercises.name: Weighted Chin-Up
steps: An underhand-grip chin-up loaded with a belt or dumbbell.
The supinated grip drives heavy biceps and lat involvement; pull from a full hang to chest and lower under control.

exercises.name: Assisted Pull-Up (Machine)
steps: A pull-up on a machine that offsets part of your bodyweight with a knee or foot platform.
Lets you build strict, full-range pulling strength toward an unassisted pull-up.

exercises.name: Band-Assisted Pull-Up
steps: A pull-up with a resistance band looped under your feet or knee for a boost out of the bottom.
The assistance fades near the top, so still finish with chin over the bar.

exercises.name: Pendlay Row
steps: A barbell row where each rep starts from a dead stop on the floor with a flat back and explosive pull to the lower chest.
Builds a powerful, strict mid-back off the ground.

exercises.name: Yates Row
steps: A barbell row with an underhand grip and a more upright ~45° torso, pulling to the waist.
The angle lets you handle heavier loads and biases the lower lats and upper back.

exercises.name: Reverse-Grip Barbell Row
steps: A bent-over barbell row with an underhand grip.
Draws the elbows tighter to the body to emphasize the lower lats and biceps; keep the back flat and pull to the belly button.

exercises.name: Chest-Supported Row
steps: A row with your chest braced on an incline bench or machine pad.
The support removes lower-back strain and cheating.
Isolating the mid-back; squeeze the shoulder blades at the top.

exercises.name: Chest-Supported Dumbbell Row
steps: Lie face-down on an incline bench and row two dumbbells up to your ribs.
The chest support forces strict form so the lats and rhomboids do all the pulling.

exercises.name: Incline Dumbbell Row
steps: Chest propped on an incline bench.
Row two dumbbells up and back with the elbows flaring slightly to hit the upper back and rear delts.
Pause and squeeze at the top.

exercises.name: Meadows Row
steps: A one-arm row on the end of a landmine barbell.
Gripping the sleeve.
The angle gives a deep lat stretch and strong contraction; brace the free hand on your knee and row to the hip.

exercises.name: Landmine Row
steps: Straddle a landmine barbell and row the loaded end to your chest with both hands or a handle.
The arc keeps constant tension on the mid-back; keep the hips hinged and back flat.

exercises.name: Machine Row
steps: A seated plate-loaded or selectorized row with a chest pad.
Pull the handles to your torso.
Driving the elbows back and squeezing the shoulder blades; a strict, back-only pull.

exercises.name: Hammer Strength Row
steps: A plate-loaded chest-supported row with independent handles.
The converging path gives a strong peak contraction; row each side evenly and pause at the squeeze.

exercises.name: Wide-Grip Seated Cable Row
steps: A seated cable row with a wide overhand bar to bias the upper back and rear delts.
Pull to the upper stomach with elbows flared and squeeze the mid-back at the finish.

exercises.name: Single-Arm Cable Row
steps: A one-arm seated cable row that lets you rotate slightly for a bigger stretch and stronger lat contraction.
Pull the handle to your hip and control the reach forward.

exercises.name: Kroc Row
steps: A high-rep, heavy one-arm dumbbell row with a little controlled body English.
Brace on a bench.
Pull hard to the hip, and chase both load and reps to build a thick back and grip.

exercises.name: Gorilla Row
steps: Hinge over two kettlebells or dumbbells on the floor and row them alternately to your hips.
The wide base and alternating pull hammer the lats while bracing the core.

exercises.name: Kettlebell Row
steps: A one-arm bent-over row with a kettlebell.
The offset load challenges grip and lets the lat stretch deep at the bottom; brace the off hand and row to the hip.

exercises.name: Resistance Band Lat Pulldown
steps: Anchor a band overhead and pull both handles down to your shoulders while kneeling or seated.
Mimics a lat pulldown at home; drive the elbows down and squeeze the lats.

exercises.name: Seal Row
steps: Lie face-down on a raised flat bench and row a barbell or dumbbells straight up to the underside.
Total chest support means zero cheating and a pure mid-back contraction.

exercises.name: Bench-Supported Dumbbell Row
steps: A one-arm dumbbell row with your free hand and knee braced on a bench.
The support keeps the back flat so the working lat does all the pulling; row to the hip and squeeze.

exercises.name: Trap Bar Deadlift
steps: A deadlift standing inside a hex/trap bar with neutral-grip handles.
The centered load is easier on the lower back and lets you lift heavy; drive through the floor and stand tall.

exercises.name: Deficit Deadlift
steps: A deadlift standing on a low platform so the bar starts below normal.
The extra range builds strength off the floor; keep a flat back through the deeper stretch.

exercises.name: Snatch-Grip Deadlift
steps: A deadlift with a very wide grip that increases the range and loads the upper back and traps hard.
Keep the chest up and the bar close as you drive to lockout.

exercises.name: Block Pull
steps: A deadlift with the bar resting on blocks or in a rack just below the knee.
Trains lockout strength through a shortened range; pull from the dead stop with a braced back.

exercises.name: Kettlebell Deadlift
steps: A deadlift lifting a kettlebell between your feet.
A joint-friendly way to groove the hip hinge; push the hips back.
Keep the back flat.
Stand tall by squeezing the glutes.

exercises.name: Hyperextension (Back Extension)
steps: On a 45° or horizontal bench.
Hinge at the hips and raise your torso in line with your legs.
Squeezing the glutes and lower back.
Don't hyperextend past a straight line.

exercises.name: 45-Degree Back Extension
steps: On an angled hyperextension bench, bend at the hips and rise until your body forms a straight line.
Targets the glutes, hamstrings, and spinal erectors; add a plate to progress.

exercises.name: Reverse Hyperextension
steps: Face-down on a bench or machine.
Swing your legs from hanging up to level behind you.
Trains the glutes and lower back with a gentle traction on the spine; control the swing.

exercises.name: Superman
steps: Lie face-down and simultaneously lift your arms, chest, and legs off the floor.
Squeezing the lower back and glutes.
Hold briefly at the top and lower with control.

exercises.name: Superman Hold
steps: The top of a Superman held as an isometric.
Arms and legs raised, back and glutes squeezed.
Building endurance in the spinal erectors; breathe and keep the neck neutral.

exercises.name: Bird Dog Row
steps: From a bird-dog position on a bench.
Row a dumbbell with one arm while bracing on the opposite knee.
Combines an anti-rotation core hold with a strict single-arm back row.

exercises.name: Inverted Row (Feet Elevated)
steps: A bodyweight row under a bar with your feet up on a box, making it harder.
Pull your chest to the bar with a rigid plank line and squeeze the shoulder blades.

exercises.name: Ring Row
steps: A bodyweight row hanging under gymnastic rings.
The free-moving rings add a stability challenge; keep a straight body and pull until the rings reach your ribs.

exercises.name: TRX Row
steps: A suspension-trainer row: lean back on the straps and pull your chest to your hands, adjusting foot position to set the difficulty.
Keep the body rigid and squeeze the mid-back.

exercises.name: Snatch-Grip High Pull
steps: Explosively pull a barbell from the hip up toward your collarbone with a wide grip and high elbows.
A powerful trap and upper-back builder; drive with the hips, not the arms.

exercises.name: Chest-Supported T-Bar Row
steps: A T-bar row with your chest braced on the machine's pad.
The support kills lower-back strain and cheating, so the mid-back and lats do all the pulling; squeeze the shoulder blades at the top.

exercises.name: Behind-the-Neck Lat Pulldown
steps: A wide-grip pulldown taken to the base of the neck instead of the collarbone.
Only worth doing if you have the shoulder mobility for it; keep the load light and the neck neutral.

exercises.name: V-Bar Lat Pulldown
steps: A pulldown using a narrow V-handle with the palms facing each other.
The neutral grip lets you pull deeper into the lats with less elbow and shoulder strain.

exercises.name: Half-Kneeling Single-Arm Lat Pulldown
steps: A one-arm cable pulldown from a half-kneeling stance.
The split position kills any body english so the lat does the pulling; keep the ribs stacked over the hips.

exercises.name: Rope Lat Pulldown
steps: A pulldown with a rope handle, splitting the hands apart as you pull past your chin.
The extra range at the bottom gives a strong lat contraction.

exercises.name: Lean-Back Lat Pulldown
steps: A wide-grip pulldown with the torso leaned back around 30 degrees, pulling the bar to the upper chest.
The angle turns it into more of a row so you can load the mid-back harder.

exercises.name: Underhand Cable Pulldown
steps: A shoulder-width pulldown with the palms facing you, driving the elbows down to your sides.
Brings the biceps and lower lats in; keep the chest tall and don't swing.

exercises.name: Archer Pull-Up
steps: A wide pull-up where you pull up and over toward one hand while the other arm stays straight.
A stepping stone to the one-arm pull-up; alternate sides each rep.

exercises.name: L-Sit Pull-Up
steps: A pull-up holding the legs straight out in front in an L shape throughout.
Adds a brutal core hold to an already hard pull; don't let the legs drift down.

exercises.name: Negative Pull-Up
steps: Jump or step to the top of a pull-up, then lower yourself over three to five seconds.
The fastest route to a first unassisted rep; end the set once you can no longer control the descent.

exercises.name: Chest-to-Bar Pull-Up
steps: A pull-up pulled high enough that the chest touches the bar.
The extra range hammers the lats and mid-back; drive the elbows back and down at the top.

exercises.name: Scapular Pull-Up
steps: Hanging with straight arms, pull the shoulder blades down and back to raise the body a few inches, then release.
Teaches the scapular control every good pull-up starts with.

exercises.name: Mixed-Grip Pull-Up
steps: A pull-up with one palm facing toward you and one away.
Noticeably easier than a strict pull-up; swap grips set to set so you don't build a lopsided pattern.

exercises.name: Tempo Pull-Up
steps: A pull-up done to a count -- two seconds up, one at the top, three down.
Removing momentum makes light bodyweight sets brutally hard and builds real control.

exercises.name: Fat-Grip Pull-Up
steps: A pull-up with thick grips, or a towel wrapped round the bar, to widen what you're holding.
A serious grip and forearm builder on top of the usual back work.

exercises.name: Close-Grip Chin-Up
steps: A chin-up with the hands only a few inches apart, palms facing you.
The narrow grip pushes even more load onto the biceps; keep the elbows in front of the body.

exercises.name: Negative Chin-Up
steps: Step to the top of a chin-up and lower over three to five seconds.
The single best way to build toward a first full chin-up.

exercises.name: Band-Assisted Chin-Up
steps: A chin-up with a resistance band under the knee or foot to offset some bodyweight.
The band helps most at the bottom, exactly where the sticking point is.

exercises.name: Assisted Chin-Up (Machine)
steps: A chin-up on an assisted pull-up machine with a counterweighted knee pad.
Dial the assistance down week to week until you can do it unassisted.

exercises.name: L-Sit Chin-Up
steps: A chin-up holding the legs out straight in an L position.
Combines a hard pull with a hard core hold; keep the legs level throughout.

exercises.name: Isometric Chin-Up Hold
steps: Hold the top of a chin-up with the chin over the bar for as long as form holds.
Builds the top-end strength that turns a grinding rep into a clean one.

exercises.name: Ring Chin-Up
steps: A chin-up on gymnastic rings, letting the hands rotate naturally through the pull.
The free rotation is much easier on the elbows than a fixed bar.

exercises.name: Towel Chin-Up
steps: A chin-up gripping two towels draped over the bar.
A savage grip and forearm builder; expect the grip to fail before the back does.

exercises.name: Tempo Chin-Up
steps: A chin-up done to a strict count, typically three seconds down.
Slowing the eccentric adds a lot of bicep and lat work at the same bodyweight.

exercises.name: Smith Machine Shrug
steps: A shrug on a Smith machine, where the fixed bar path lets you focus purely on driving the traps up.
Pause at the top and lower slowly; don't roll the shoulders.

exercises.name: Machine Shrug
steps: A shrug on a dedicated shrug machine with padded handles.
Constant tension and no grip limitation, so the traps take the whole set.

exercises.name: Incline Dumbbell Shrug
steps: A shrug lying chest-down on an incline bench with dumbbells hanging.
The angle shifts the work to the mid traps and rhomboids rather than the upper traps.

exercises.name: Snatch-Grip Shrug
steps: A barbell shrug taken with a very wide, snatch-width grip.
The wide hands bias the upper back and traps; keep the bar close to the body.

exercises.name: Kettlebell Shrug
steps: A shrug holding a kettlebell in each hand at your sides.
The lower centre of mass makes the grip work harder; drive the traps straight up, not back.

exercises.name: Resistance Band Shrug
steps: Stand on a band with a handle in each hand and shrug the shoulders straight up.
Tension rises as you shrug, so squeeze hard at the top.

exercises.name: Single-Arm Dumbbell Shrug
steps: A shrug with one heavy dumbbell, the free hand steadying you on a rack.
Lets you load one side properly and gives the core an anti-side-bend job.

exercises.name: Prone Shrug (Chest-Supported)
steps: Face-down on an incline bench, shrug the shoulder blades together and up.
Isolates the mid and lower traps with zero low-back involvement.

exercises.name: Overhead Barbell Shrug
steps: Hold a barbell locked out overhead and shrug the shoulders up toward the ears.
Builds the overhead-support strength that carries into pressing and the Olympic lifts.

exercises.name: Banded Good Morning
steps: A good morning with a band looped behind the neck and under the feet.
Tension peaks at lockout, so it hammers the glutes and hamstrings with no spinal loading.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Good Morning
steps: A good morning holding a single dumbbell against the chest or on the upper back.
A lighter, more accessible way to learn the hinge; keep the back flat and push the hips back.

exercises.name: Safety Bar Good Morning
steps: A good morning with a safety squat bar, whose handles and padding keep the shoulders comfortable.
Lets you load the hinge heavier without shoulder strain.

exercises.name: Single-Leg Good Morning
steps: A good morning balanced on one leg with the other extended behind.
A hamstring and balance builder; go light and keep the hips square.

exercises.name: Wide-Stance Good Morning
steps: A barbell good morning with the feet set well outside shoulder width.
The wide stance brings the adductors and glutes in alongside the hamstrings.

exercises.name: Kneeling Face Pull
steps: A cable face pull from a tall-kneeling position.
Taking the legs out of it stops you leaning back and keeps the rear delts honest.

exercises.name: Seated Face Pull
steps: A face pull done seated at a cable station with the rope at head height.
The fixed torso means every bit of the pull comes from the rear delts and mid-back.

exercises.name: Single-Arm Face Pull
steps: A one-armed cable face pull, pulling the handle toward the same-side ear.
The extra rotation at the end gives the rear delt a stronger squeeze.

exercises.name: High Cable Face Pull
steps: A face pull with the pulley above head height, pulling down and back toward the forehead.
Biases the lower traps as well as the rear delts.

exercises.name: Low Cable Face Pull
steps: A face pull from a low pulley, pulling up and back toward the face.
The upward angle shifts the work toward the upper back; keep the elbows high.

exercises.name: Prone Dumbbell Face Pull
steps: Face-down on an incline bench, pull two light dumbbells back toward your ears with the elbows high.
A cable-free rear delt option; go light and pause at the top.

exercises.name: Shoulder Press
steps: Press the weight straight overhead from shoulder height until your arms lock out.
Keeping your core braced so your lower back doesn't arch to help push the weight up.

exercises.name: Overhead Press
steps: The standing barbell version of a shoulder press.
Brace your glutes and abs hard.
Press the bar in a straight line, and move your head slightly back then forward as the bar clears your face.

exercises.name: Arnold Press
steps: Start with dumbbells in front of your shoulders, palms facing you.
Rotate your palms outward as you press overhead.
The rotation adds extra shoulder engagement, so keep the weight moderate.

exercises.name: Lateral Raise
steps: With a soft bend in your elbows.
Raise the dumbbells out to your sides until they're roughly shoulder height.
Leading with your elbows rather than your hands.
Avoid swinging the weight up with momentum.

exercises.name: Cable Lateral Raise
steps: Same raising motion as a dumbbell lateral raise but using a low cable pulley, which keeps constant tension on the side delt through the whole range of motion.

exercises.name: Front Raise
steps: Raise the weight straight in front of you to about shoulder height with a slight elbow bend.
Avoid using your legs or lower back to heave the weight upward.

exercises.name: Rear Delt Fly
steps: Hinged forward at the hips.
Raise the dumbbells out to the sides focusing on squeezing your rear shoulders and upper back together.
Keeping the movement slow and controlled rather than swinging.

exercises.name: Face Pull
steps: Pull a rope attachment toward your face at eye level, flaring your elbows out wide and rotating your hands so your knuckles finish pointing behind you.
Great for shoulder health, so prioritize control over heavy weight.

exercises.name: Resistance Band Face Pull
steps: Same motion as a cable face pull.
Using a band anchored at eye level instead.
Pull toward your face while flaring your elbows wide, finishing with your knuckles pointing behind you.

exercises.name: Upright Row
steps: Pull the bar or handle straight up along your torso to roughly chest height.
Leading with your elbows.
Stop before your elbows go above shoulder height to protect your shoulder joints.

exercises.name: Shrug
steps: Holding weight at your sides.
Lift your shoulders straight up toward your ears without rolling them forward or back.
Pause briefly at the top.
Lower under control.

exercises.name: Pike Push-Up
steps: Hips piked up so your body forms an inverted V, hands on the floor under your shoulders.
Lower the crown of your head toward the floor by bending your elbows.
Press back up; a bodyweight-only shoulder press substitute.

exercises.name: Seated Dumbbell Shoulder Press
steps: Seated with back support.
Press two dumbbells overhead until the arms are nearly locked.
Lower to ear level.
The seat removes leg drive so the delts do the work.

exercises.name: Standing Dumbbell Shoulder Press
steps: Press two dumbbells overhead from the shoulders while standing, bracing the core so you don't lean back.
A strict overhead press that also trains full-body stability.

exercises.name: Seated Barbell Shoulder Press
steps: Seated.
Press a barbell from your upper chest to overhead in a straight line.
The bench support lets you overload the delts; keep the ribs down and don't arch excessively.

exercises.name: Machine Shoulder Press
steps: A seated overhead press machine with a fixed path.
Press the handles up and slightly in, stopping short of lockout to keep the delts under tension; great for pushing to failure safely.

exercises.name: Smith Machine Shoulder Press
steps: An overhead press on the Smith machine's guided bar, seated or standing.
The fixed track handles balance so you can focus on driving straight up and controlling the descent.

exercises.name: Push Press
steps: An overhead press using a slight dip and drive of the legs to launch the bar.
Locking it out with the shoulders.
Lets you move heavier loads and builds overhead power.

exercises.name: Z Press
steps: An overhead press seated on the floor with legs straight out.
The position removes all leg and back support, forcing a strict press and a very stable core; start light.

exercises.name: Behind-the-Neck Press
steps: A barbell overhead press lowered behind the head to the base of the neck.
Demands good shoulder mobility, so go light and only descend as far as stays comfortable.

exercises.name: Single-Arm Dumbbell Shoulder Press
steps: A one-arm overhead press with a dumbbell.
Pressing one side adds an anti-lean core demand and evens out imbalances; keep the torso upright and don't tip toward the weight.

exercises.name: Single-Arm Landmine Press
steps: Press the end of a landmine barbell overhead and forward with one arm.
The arc is shoulder-friendly and hits the front delt while the core resists rotation.

exercises.name: Bradford Press
steps: A barbell press alternating in front of and behind the head, never locking out.
The constant tension torches the delts; use a light load and keep the reps smooth.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Lateral Raise
steps: Raise two dumbbells out to the sides to shoulder height with a slight elbow bend.
Leading with the elbows.
The classic side-delt builder; control the lower and don't swing.

exercises.name: Seated Lateral Raise
steps: A lateral raise done seated to remove momentum.
Lift the dumbbells out to the sides strictly to shoulder height.
Pause.
Lower slowly for maximum side-delt tension.

exercises.name: Leaning Cable Lateral Raise
steps: Hold a post and lean away from a low cable, raising the handle out to the side.
Leaning increases the range and keeps tension on the side delt from the very bottom.

exercises.name: Machine Lateral Raise
steps: A seated machine that pads against your upper arms as you raise them out to the sides.
The fixed path isolates the side delts and is easy to push to failure.

exercises.name: Lu Raise
steps: Raise two dumbbells from your sides all the way overhead in a wide arc with straight-ish arms.
A full-range side and front delt move; keep it light and controlled throughout.

exercises.name: Cable Front Raise
steps: Raise a low-cable handle straight out in front to shoulder height.
The cable keeps tension on the front delt through the whole range, unlike a dumbbell that unloads at the bottom.

exercises.name: Plate Front Raise
steps: Hold a weight plate at the edges and raise it straight out in front to eye level.
A simple front-delt builder; keep the arms straight and avoid rocking the torso.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Front Raise
steps: Raise a dumbbell straight out in front to shoulder height, one arm at a time or together, to target the front delt.
Keep a slight elbow bend and don't use momentum.

exercises.name: Bent-Over Dumbbell Rear Delt Fly
steps: Hinge forward and open two dumbbells out to the sides with a soft elbow bend.
Squeezing the rear delts and upper back.
Lead with the elbows and don't let it turn into a row.

exercises.name: Seated Rear Delt Fly
steps: Seated and bent forward over your thighs, fly two dumbbells out to the sides to isolate the rear delts.
The seated position kills momentum for a stricter contraction.

exercises.name: Cable Rear Delt Fly
steps: Using a high or shoulder-height cable across the body.
Sweep the handle out and back to hit the rear delt with constant tension.
Squeeze the shoulder blade and control the return.

exercises.name: Reverse Pec Deck
steps: Sit facing the pec-deck machine and open the handles out and back to target the rear delts and upper back.
Keep the chest against the pad and squeeze the shoulder blades together.

exercises.name: Rear Delt Row
steps: A high-elbow row (barbell, dumbbells, or cable) pulled to the upper chest with flared elbows to bias the rear delts and upper back over the lats.
Pause and squeeze at the top.

exercises.name: Cable Face Pull (Rope)
steps: Pull a rope from a high pulley toward your face, splitting the ends past your ears with the elbows high.
A rear-delt and rotator-cuff staple for shoulder health; squeeze at the end.

exercises.name: Y-Raise
steps: Raise two light dumbbells up and out into a 'Y' overhead with thumbs up.
Targets the lower traps and rear/side delts; keep the arms straight and lift only as high as stays smooth.

exercises.name: Prone Y-Raise
steps: Face-down on an incline bench.
Raise two light dumbbells into a 'Y' overhead.
Strengthens the lower traps and posture muscles with strict, momentum-free reps.

exercises.name: W-Raise
steps: Face-down or leaning.
Pull two light dumbbells back into a 'W' shape by driving the elbows down and squeezing the shoulder blades.
A rear-delt and lower-trap posture drill.

exercises.name: Cuban Press
steps: A three-part move: upright-row the dumbbells up, externally rotate them so the forearms point up.
Press overhead.
A rotator-cuff and shoulder-health builder; go light.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Upright Row
steps: Pull two dumbbells straight up the front of the body to chest height with the elbows leading high.
Hits the side delts and traps; keep the lift to below the collarbone to spare the shoulders.

exercises.name: Cable Upright Row
steps: Pull a low-cable bar or rope up the front of the body with high elbows.
The cable keeps steady tension on the delts and traps; stop the pull at upper-chest height.

exercises.name: Wide-Grip Upright Row
steps: An upright row with a wide barbell grip that biases the side delts over the traps and keeps the shoulders in a safer position.
Pull to chest height with the elbows out.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Shrug
steps: Hold a dumbbell in each hand and shrug the shoulders straight up toward your ears.
Squeezing the traps at the top.
Lower fully.
No rolling; just straight up and down.

exercises.name: Barbell Shrug
steps: Hold a barbell at arm's length and shrug the shoulders up to your ears.
Pausing to squeeze the traps.
Keep the arms straight and avoid rolling the shoulders forward or back.

exercises.name: Cable Shrug
steps: Shrug against a low cable or bar attachment.
The constant tension keeps the traps loaded through the whole range; lift straight up.
Squeeze.
Lower under control.

exercises.name: Trap Bar Shrug
steps: Shrug while holding a loaded trap/hex bar.
The neutral-grip, centered load lets you shrug heavy and safely; drive the shoulders straight up and pause at the top.

exercises.name: Behind-the-Back Barbell Shrug
steps: Hold a barbell behind your glutes and shrug straight up.
The rear position pulls the shoulders back and hits the traps with better posture; squeeze hard at the top.

exercises.name: Handstand Push-Up
steps: A vertical push-up kicked up against a wall.
A bodyweight overhead press for the delts and triceps; lower under control until your head nears the floor.
Press back up.

exercises.name: Wall Handstand Hold
steps: Kick up to a handstand against a wall and hold, building overhead and shoulder stability plus core control.
Keep the ribs down and press the floor away through the shoulders.

exercises.name: Pike Press (Deficit)
steps: A pike push-up with hands on raised blocks so your head drops below them.
The added range makes it a tougher bodyweight overhead press for the shoulders; control the descent.

exercises.name: Landmine Lateral Raise
steps: Raise the end of a landmine barbell out to the side with one arm.
The fixed arc keeps steady tension on the side delt through a controlled range; alternate sides.

exercises.name: 3-Way Shoulder Raise
steps: A giant set flowing front raise into lateral raise into bent-over rear raise with light dumbbells.
Hits all three delt heads in one continuous, high-tension sequence.

exercises.name: Cable Y-Raise
steps: From low pulleys crossed in front.
Raise both handles up and out into a 'Y' overhead.
The constant cable tension hits the side and rear delts plus lower traps; keep the arms long and thumbs up.

exercises.name: Barbell Upright Row
steps: An upright row with a barbell pulled to chest height, elbows leading.
Use a slightly wider grip and stop below the collarbone to keep the shoulders happy.

exercises.name: Smith Machine Upright Row
steps: An upright row on a Smith machine, where the fixed path removes any swing.
Lead with the elbows and stop the pull at chest height.

exercises.name: Kettlebell Upright Row
steps: An upright row with one or two kettlebells hanging close to the body.
The bells sit closer to your centre than dumbbells, which keeps the path tight.

exercises.name: Resistance Band Upright Row
steps: Stand on a band and row the handles up to chest height with high elbows.
A joint-friendly way to train the traps and side delts at home.

exercises.name: Single-Arm Cable Upright Row
steps: A one-armed upright row from a low pulley.
The cable keeps tension through the whole pull and lets each side move naturally.

exercises.name: Close-Grip Upright Row
steps: An upright row with the hands close together, biasing the traps over the delts.
The narrow grip is harder on the shoulders -- keep the range short and the weight moderate.

exercises.name: Snatch-Grip Upright Row
steps: A very wide-grip upright row, more of a high pull than a shrug.
The width takes strain off the shoulder joint and hits the rear and side delts.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Upright Row (Single-Arm)
steps: An upright row with one dumbbell at a time, free hand on a bench for support.
Lets you groove a cleaner path on each side; keep the elbow above the hand.

exercises.name: Landmine Upright Row
steps: An upright row on the end of a landmine barbell, whose arc keeps the shoulders in a friendlier path.
Pull the end of the bar to chest height and lower under control.

exercises.name: Cable Rope Upright Row
steps: An upright row with a rope on a low pulley, letting the hands split as the elbows rise.
The free hand position is much kinder to the wrists and shoulders.

exercises.name: Bicep Curl
steps: Keeping your elbows pinned to your sides.
Curl the weight up by bending your elbow only.
Avoid swinging your torso or letting your upper arm drift forward to cheat the weight up.

exercises.name: Barbell Bicep Curl
steps: Same curl motion as a dumbbell curl.
Gripping a straight barbell with both hands.
Lets you load more total weight than dumbbells.
Keep your elbows pinned and don't lean back to heave it up.

exercises.name: EZ-Bar Bicep Curl
steps: A barbell curl using a zigzag-shaped EZ-bar instead of a straight one.
The angled grip is easier on the wrists, especially at heavier loads, while training the same strict elbow-only curling motion.

exercises.name: Resistance Band Bicep Curl
steps: Stand on the middle of a resistance band.
Holding a handle in each hand.
Curl up against the band's tension.
The resistance gets harder the higher you curl, unlike a dumbbell where gravity does the opposite.

exercises.name: Hammer Curl
steps: Same curling motion as a bicep curl but with palms facing each other the whole time (like holding a hammer).
This shifts more emphasis onto the forearm and outer arm muscle.

exercises.name: Preacher Curl
steps: With your upper arms braced against an angled pad.
Curl the weight up.
The pad prevents cheating with momentum, so use a weight you can control through the full stretch at the bottom.

exercises.name: Concentration Curl
steps: Seated.
Brace your elbow against your inner thigh and curl the dumbbell up in a strict, isolated arc.
A slow, controlled tempo matters more than the weight used here.

exercises.name: Cable Curl
steps: Curl a bar or handle attached to a low pulley.
The cable keeps tension on your biceps even at the bottom of the rep, unlike a dumbbell or barbell curl.

exercises.name: Spider Curl
steps: Lying chest-down on an incline bench with your arms hanging straight down.
Curl the weight up.
This position removes any ability to swing your body.
Isolating the biceps hard.

exercises.name: Zottman Curl
steps: Curl the dumbbells up with palms facing up like a normal curl.
Rotate your wrists to face down before lowering.
The reversed lowering phase works your forearms extra.

exercises.name: Tricep Pushdown
steps: Keeping your elbows pinned to your sides.
Push a bar or rope attachment straight down until your arms are fully extended.
Control it back up without letting your elbows flare out.

exercises.name: Tricep Extension
steps: With a dumbbell held overhead in both hands.
Lower it behind your head by bending only at the elbow.
Extend back up.
Keep your upper arms still and close to your ears.

exercises.name: Overhead Tricep Extension
steps: Same movement as a tricep extension, performed strictly overhead.
Brace your core to avoid arching your lower back as the weight moves behind your head.

exercises.name: Barbell Skull Crusher
steps: Same lying-tricep-extension motion as a skull crusher.
Using a straight or EZ-bar instead of a dumbbell.
Lets you load more weight.
Keep the lowering phase slow and controlled since a bar over your face has zero margin for error.

exercises.name: Skull Crusher
steps: Lying on a bench with the weight held straight above your chest.
Lower it toward your forehead by bending only your elbows.
Press back up.
Despite the name, this should stay slow and controlled, not crash toward your head.

exercises.name: Close-Grip Bench Press
steps: A bench press with your hands just inside shoulder width.
Keeping your elbows tucked close to your body as you lower the bar to your lower chest.
This shifts more of the work onto your triceps.

exercises.name: Diamond Push-Up
steps: A push-up with your hands close together under your chest, forming a diamond shape with your thumbs and index fingers.
A harder, more tricep-focused variation of a standard push-up.

exercises.name: Bench Dip
steps: Hands on the edge of a bench behind you, legs extended out in front.
Lower your hips toward the floor by bending your elbows.
Press back up.
A bodyweight tricep move that needs nothing but a bench or sturdy chair.

exercises.name: Cable Kickback
steps: Hinged forward with your upper arm held still and parallel to the floor.
Extend your forearm straight back against cable resistance.
Squeezing your tricep at full extension.

exercises.name: Incline Dumbbell Curl
steps: Lie back on an incline bench and curl two dumbbells with the arms hanging behind the body.
The stretched starting position hits the long head of the biceps hard; no swinging.

exercises.name: Seated Dumbbell Curl
steps: Curl two dumbbells while seated to remove momentum.
The strict position forces the biceps to lift the weight without help from the legs or a body swing.

exercises.name: Standing Dumbbell Curl
steps: Curl two dumbbells from your sides up to your shoulders.
Keeping the elbows pinned.
Supinate (turn the pinky up) at the top for a full biceps contraction; lower slowly.

exercises.name: Alternating Dumbbell Curl
steps: Curl one dumbbell at a time, alternating arms, so you can focus on each biceps in turn.
Keep the non-working arm still and avoid rocking the torso to swing the weight.

exercises.name: Cross-Body Hammer Curl
steps: Curl a dumbbell across your body toward the opposite shoulder with a neutral grip.
Targets the brachialis and forearm; keep the elbow tucked and alternate arms.

exercises.name: Incline Hammer Curl
steps: On an incline bench.
Curl two dumbbells with a neutral (palms-facing) grip from the stretched hanging position.
Hits the brachialis and outer arm with a big stretch.

exercises.name: Rope Hammer Curl
steps: Curl a rope attachment on a low cable with a neutral grip.
Keeping the palms facing in.
The constant cable tension builds the brachialis and forearms; squeeze at the top.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Preacher Curl
steps: Curl one dumbbell with the back of your arm braced on a preacher bench pad.
The fixed angle eliminates cheating and puts deep tension on the lower biceps; control the stretch.

exercises.name: Machine Preacher Curl
steps: A seated machine curl with the arms braced on a pad.
The guided path isolates the biceps and is easy to push to failure; get a full stretch at the bottom and squeeze at the top.

exercises.name: Machine Bicep Curl
steps: A seated selectorized curl with the elbows fixed on a pad.
The machine keeps the arms locked in position for strict, momentum-free biceps work through a full range.

exercises.name: Single-Arm Cable Curl
steps: Curl a single low-cable handle with one arm.
The cable keeps tension on the biceps through the whole range, and going one side at a time evens out arm imbalances.

exercises.name: High Cable Curl
steps: Stand between two high pulleys and curl both handles toward your head like a front double-biceps pose.
The overhead angle peaks the biceps contraction; squeeze hard.

exercises.name: Bayesian Cable Curl
steps: Face away from a low pulley and curl the handle with your arm behind the body.
The constant-tension stretch position is one of the best long-head biceps builders.

exercises.name: Drag Curl
steps: Curl a barbell or dumbbells by dragging them straight up the front of the body while the elbows travel back.
A strict variation that keeps constant tension on the biceps.

exercises.name: Reverse Curl
steps: Curl a barbell or dumbbells with an overhand (pronated) grip.
Shifts the work to the brachialis and forearm extensors for thicker, stronger-looking arms; keep the wrists firm.

exercises.name: Reverse EZ-Bar Curl
steps: A reverse (overhand) curl on an EZ-bar, whose angled grip is easier on the wrists.
Builds the forearms and brachialis; keep the elbows pinned and lift without swinging.

exercises.name: Cable Reverse Curl
steps: An overhand-grip curl on a low cable bar.
The steady tension hammers the forearm extensors and brachialis; keep the wrists neutral and the elbows tight to the body.

exercises.name: 21s Bicep Curl
steps: A curl set of seven bottom-half reps, seven top-half reps.
Seven full reps for 21 total.
The extended time under tension gives the biceps a deep pump; use a lighter load.

exercises.name: Waiter Curl
steps: Curl a single dumbbell held vertically by the top end in both cupped hands, like carrying a tray.
The grip forces a strong biceps peak contraction; squeeze hard at the top.

exercises.name: Resistance Band Hammer Curl
steps: Stand on a band and curl the handles with a neutral grip.
The band's rising tension peaks the brachialis contraction at the top; keep the elbows pinned and squeeze.

exercises.name: Isometric Bicep Hold
steps: Hold a curl at the mid-range (elbow ~90°) with a challenging weight for time.
The static contraction builds biceps strength and endurance; keep the elbow pinned and breathe.

exercises.name: Rope Tricep Pushdown
steps: Push a rope down from a high pulley, splitting the ends apart at the bottom and locking out the elbows.
The rope split maximizes the triceps squeeze; keep the elbows tucked.

exercises.name: V-Bar Tricep Pushdown
steps: Push a V-bar down from a high pulley to full lockout.
The fixed grip lets you load the triceps heavier than a rope; keep the elbows pinned to your sides throughout.

exercises.name: Single-Arm Tricep Pushdown
steps: A one-arm cable pushdown with a handle, often with an underhand grip.
Isolates each triceps and evens out imbalances; keep the elbow glued to your side and fully extend.

exercises.name: Reverse-Grip Tricep Pushdown
steps: A cable pushdown with an underhand (supinated) grip on a straight bar.
Biases the inner/medial head of the triceps; keep the wrists firm and the elbows locked in place.

exercises.name: Cable Overhead Tricep Extension
steps: Face away from a high or low pulley and extend a rope overhead until the arms lock out.
The overhead angle stretches and works the long head of the triceps; keep the elbows narrow.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Overhead Tricep Extension
steps: Hold a dumbbell overhead in one or both hands and lower it behind your head.
Extend to lockout.
The overhead stretch targets the long head; keep the elbows pointing forward.

exercises.name: Single-Arm Overhead Tricep Extension
steps: Extend a single dumbbell overhead with one arm.
Lowering it behind the head and pressing to lockout.
Isolates each triceps and evens out imbalances; keep the elbow still and high.

exercises.name: EZ-Bar Overhead Extension
steps: Press an EZ-bar overhead and lower it behind your head.
Extend to lockout.
The angled grip is wrist-friendly and the overhead position loads the long head of the triceps.

exercises.name: Lying Dumbbell Tricep Extension
steps: Lying on a bench.
Lower two dumbbells toward your forehead or beside your head.
Extend to lockout.
A dumbbell skull crusher that hits all three triceps heads; keep the elbows in.

exercises.name: Cable Skull Crusher
steps: Lying on a bench with a low cable.
Lower a bar or rope toward your forehead and extend.
The cable keeps constant tension on the triceps that a barbell loses at lockout.

exercises.name: EZ-Bar Skull Crusher
steps: Lying down.
Lower an EZ-bar to your forehead or just behind your head by bending only the elbows.
Extend.
The angled bar spares the wrists; keep the upper arms still.

exercises.name: JM Press
steps: A hybrid of a close-grip bench and skull crusher.
Lower the bar toward your upper neck with the elbows tucked.
Press back.
A heavy triceps builder; start light to groove it.

exercises.name: Tate Press
steps: Lying down.
Lower two dumbbells with the elbows flared so the weights come toward your chest.
Extend.
An unusual angle that hammers the outer triceps; keep it light and strict.

exercises.name: Tricep Dip (Bench, Weighted)
steps: A bench dip with feet elevated and a plate on your lap for added load.
Keep the elbows tucked and the torso upright to bias the triceps; lower until the elbows hit ~90°.

exercises.name: Tricep Kickback
steps: Hinge forward, pin the upper arm to your side.
Extend a dumbbell straight back to lockout.
Squeeze the triceps hard at the top; the peak contraction is the whole point, so go light.

exercises.name: Cable Tricep Kickback
steps: A one-arm kickback on a low cable.
The constant tension keeps the triceps loaded even at full lockout, unlike a dumbbell; keep the upper arm pinned and horizontal.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Tricep Kickback
steps: Braced on a bench.
Extend a dumbbell back from a pinned upper arm until the elbow locks out.
A strict single-arm triceps isolation; squeeze and hold briefly at the top.

exercises.name: Katana Tricep Extension
steps: Face away from a high pulley and extend a single handle down and across your body like drawing a sword.
A constant-tension single-arm triceps move; keep the elbow high and still.

exercises.name: Resistance Band Tricep Pushdown
steps: Anchor a band up high and push the handles down to lockout.
The band's tension peaks at full extension.
Squeezing the triceps hard; keep the elbows pinned to your sides.

exercises.name: Resistance Band Overhead Extension
steps: Anchor a band low, face away.
Extend the handles overhead to lockout.
The overhead stretch and rising band tension load the long head of the triceps; keep the elbows narrow.

exercises.name: California Press
steps: A blend of a close-grip bench and a skull crusher: lower the bar to your chin/upper chest half like a skull crusher.
Press out.
A heavy, joint-friendly triceps builder.

exercises.name: Wrist Curl
steps: Rest your forearms on your thighs or a bench with palms up and curl the weight using only the wrists.
Isolates the forearm flexors; use a full range and a light, controlled load.

exercises.name: Reverse Wrist Curl
steps: Forearms braced with palms down.
Raise the weight using only the wrists.
Targets the forearm extensors for balanced, injury-resistant forearms; keep the movement slow and small.

exercises.name: Behind-the-Back Wrist Curl
steps: Hold a barbell behind your glutes and curl it with the wrists.
The position gives the forearm flexors a bigger range than a standard wrist curl; keep it light and controlled.

exercises.name: Cable Wrist Curl
steps: Curl a low-cable bar using only the wrists with the forearms braced.
The constant tension keeps the forearm flexors loaded throughout; slow and controlled beats heavy here.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Wrist Curl
steps: A single-arm wrist curl with a dumbbell, forearm braced on your thigh.
Lets each forearm work independently through a full flex-and-extend range; keep it slow and light.

exercises.name: Farmer's Hold
steps: Hold a heavy dumbbell or kettlebell in each hand and simply stand tall for time.
A static grip, forearm, and trap builder; keep the shoulders back and brace the core.

exercises.name: Plate Pinch Hold
steps: Pinch one or two smooth weight plates between your fingers and thumb and hold for time.
A brutal grip and thumb-strength builder; set a target time and beat it each session.

exercises.name: Wrist Roller
steps: Roll a weight up on a cord wrapped around a bar or handle using only wrist rotation.
Lower it.
A classic forearm-burner; do it both directions for balanced grip strength.

exercises.name: Hand Gripper Squeeze
steps: Squeeze a spring hand gripper closed for reps or holds.
A simple, portable crushing-grip builder; work both hands evenly and control the release, don't let it snap open.

exercises.name: Fat-Grip Dumbbell Hold
steps: Wrap thick grips (or a towel) around a dumbbell handle and hold for time.
The enlarged diameter massively increases the grip and forearm demand; keep the shoulders packed.

exercises.name: Towel Pull-Up Hold
steps: Drape a towel over a bar.
Grip an end in each hand, and hang or hold at the top of a pull-up.
A savage grip and forearm challenge; keep the core tight and shoulders active.

exercises.name: Dead Hang
steps: Simply hang from a pull-up bar with straight arms for time.
Builds grip endurance and decompresses the shoulders and spine; keep the shoulders slightly active, not fully slack.

exercises.name: Finger Curl
steps: Let a barbell or dumbbells roll to your fingertips.
Curl them back into your palm using only the fingers.
Targets the deep grip and forearm flexors; keep the load light.

exercises.name: Spider Hammer Curl
steps: Lean chest-down on an incline bench and curl a dumbbell with a neutral grip, the arm hanging straight down.
The position kills momentum and hammers the brachialis; squeeze at the top.

exercises.name: Rope Overhead Tricep Extension
steps: Facing away from a low pulley with a rope overhead, extend the elbows until the arms lock out.
The overhead position stretches the long head of the tricep hardest.

exercises.name: Single-Arm Cable Tricep Extension
steps: A one-armed cable extension, either overhead or down at your side.
Lets you fix a weaker side and keeps constant tension through the whole range.

exercises.name: Machine Tricep Extension
steps: A seated tricep extension machine with the elbows fixed on a pad.
No stabilising demand at all, so you can push the triceps close to failure safely.

exercises.name: Incline Dumbbell Tricep Extension
steps: A lying tricep extension on an incline bench, lowering the dumbbells past the head.
The angle increases the stretch on the long head; keep the elbows pointed at the ceiling.

exercises.name: Bodyweight Tricep Extension
steps: Set a bar or suspension straps at waist height and lower your forehead toward it by bending only at the elbows.
A brutal bodyweight tricep builder; raise the bar to make it easier.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Skull Crusher
steps: A lying tricep extension with a dumbbell in each hand, lowering to either side of the head.
The independent hands are easier on the elbows than a fixed bar.

exercises.name: Incline Skull Crusher
steps: A skull crusher on an incline bench, which keeps tension on the triceps at lockout.
Lower slowly toward the forehead and stop just short of full extension.

exercises.name: Decline Skull Crusher
steps: A skull crusher on a decline bench, lowering the bar behind the head.
The decline keeps the triceps loaded through a longer range.

exercises.name: Single-Arm Skull Crusher
steps: A one-armed lying tricep extension with a dumbbell.
Great for evening out arms and for feeling the tricep work in isolation.

exercises.name: Rope Skull Crusher
steps: A lying skull crusher performed with a rope attached to a low pulley behind you.
Constant cable tension makes the lockout the hardest part; split the rope at the top.

exercises.name: Smith Machine Skull Crusher
steps: A skull crusher on a Smith machine bar, whose fixed path removes any wobble.
Ideal for pushing close to failure without a spotter.

exercises.name: Single-Arm Cable Tricep Kickback
steps: A kickback from a low pulley, hinged forward with the upper arm pinned to your side.
Cable tension holds at lockout, where a dumbbell kickback gives up.

exercises.name: Banded Tricep Kickback
steps: A kickback against a band anchored in front of you.
Resistance rises as the arm straightens, so squeeze hard at lockout.

exercises.name: Bent-Over Dumbbell Kickback (Both Arms)
steps: A tricep kickback with both arms at once, hinged forward at about 45 degrees.
Keep the upper arms glued to your sides and move only at the elbows.

exercises.name: Incline Dumbbell Bicep Curl
steps: A curl seated back on an incline bench with the arms hanging behind the body.
The stretched start position is one of the best long-head bicep builders.

exercises.name: Preacher Bicep Curl
steps: A curl with the upper arms resting on a preacher pad.
The pad removes all swing so the biceps take the whole set; don't fully lock out at the bottom.

exercises.name: Cable Bicep Curl
steps: A standing curl on a low pulley with a straight or EZ attachment.
Constant tension top to bottom, unlike a dumbbell that unloads at the top.

exercises.name: Seated Dumbbell Bicep Curl
steps: A dumbbell curl performed seated upright on a bench.
Sitting kills the hip drive people use to cheat standing curls.

exercises.name: Reverse-Grip Bicep Curl
steps: A curl with the palms facing down throughout.
Shifts the work to the brachialis and forearms; expect to use noticeably less weight.

exercises.name: Cross-Body Bicep Curl
steps: A hammer-grip curl brought diagonally across the body toward the opposite shoulder.
Hits the brachialis hard and builds arm thickness.

exercises.name: Drag Bicep Curl
steps: A curl where the bar is dragged straight up the torso with the elbows travelling backward.
Keeps tension on the biceps and takes the front delts out of it.

exercises.name: Spider Bicep Curl
steps: A curl lying chest-down on an incline bench with the arms hanging straight down.
The arms-forward position makes the peak contraction the hardest part.

exercises.name: Squat
steps: Feet shoulder-width, bar on your upper back.
Sit your hips down and back while keeping your chest up and knees tracking over your toes.
Go as deep as your mobility allows without your lower back rounding.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Squat
steps: Same squat pattern as a barbell squat.
Holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides (or one at your chest) instead of a bar on your back.
A no-rack way to load a squat at home, at the cost of less total weight than a barbell allows.

exercises.name: Front Squat
steps: Same squat pattern with the bar racked across the front of your shoulders instead of your back.
This demands a more upright torso and shifts more emphasis onto your quads.

exercises.name: Goblet Squat
steps: Hold a single dumbbell or kettlebell vertically against your chest and squat down between your knees.
A beginner-friendly squat pattern since the front-loaded weight naturally keeps your torso upright.

exercises.name: Sumo Squat
steps: A wide stance with toes turned out, squatting straight down between your legs.
Targets your inner thighs and glutes more than a standard-stance squat.

exercises.name: Box Squat
steps: Squat down until you lightly touch a box or bench behind you.
Pause briefly without relaxing.
Drive back up.
Great for learning to sit your hips back properly and controlling depth.

exercises.name: Pistol Squat
steps: A single-leg squat with your other leg extended straight out in front.
Lower under control until your hips are near your heel.
Drive back up; an advanced bodyweight move that needs real ankle mobility and balance before loading it further.

exercises.name: Leg Press
steps: Feet shoulder-width on the platform.
Lower the weight until your knees reach about 90°.
Press back up without locking your knees out hard or letting your lower back round off the pad.

exercises.name: Hack Squat
steps: On the angled hack squat machine with your back against the pad.
Lower under control until your knees reach roughly 90°.
Press back up.
Keep your heels flat throughout.

exercises.name: Leg Extension
steps: Seated on the machine.
Extend your legs to straighten your knees against the pad resistance.
Lower under control.
An isolation move for the quads, not a pressing movement.

exercises.name: Lying Leg Curl Machine
steps: Lying face-down on the machine.
Curl your heels toward your glutes against the pad resistance.
Lower slowly.
Avoid lifting your hips off the bench to cheat the weight up.

exercises.name: Seated Leg Curl
steps: Seated on the machine with the pad against your lower shins.
Curl your heels down and back underneath the seat.
Focusing on squeezing your hamstrings at the bottom.

exercises.name: Nordic Hamstring Curl
steps: Kneeling with your ankles anchored.
Lower your torso forward as slowly as possible using only your hamstrings to control the descent.
A very advanced, injury-prevention-focused hamstring exercise, so build up gradually.

exercises.name: Walking Lunge
steps: Step forward into a lunge.
Lowering your back knee toward the floor.
Push off your front foot into the next step.
Keep your torso upright and your front knee tracking over your ankle, not caving inward.

exercises.name: Reverse Lunge
steps: Step backward into a lunge instead of forward.
Generally easier on the knees than a walking or forward lunge since there's less forward momentum to control.

exercises.name: Bulgarian Split Squat
steps: With your rear foot elevated on a bench behind you.
Lower straight down on your front leg until your back knee nearly touches the floor.
Drive back up.
Most of the work should be felt in your front leg, not your back foot.

exercises.name: Step-Up
steps: Step fully onto a box or bench with one foot.
Driving through your heel to stand up on top rather than pushing off your trailing leg.
Control the step back down instead of just dropping.

exercises.name: Hip Thrust
steps: With your upper back braced on a bench and a bar across your hips.
Drive your hips up until your body forms a straight line from shoulders to knees.
Squeezing your glutes hard at the top.

exercises.name: Barbell Hip Thrust
steps: The full-weight-room hip thrust: upper back braced on a bench, a padded barbell across your hips.
Driving your hips up to a straight line from shoulders to knees.
