Lets you load far more weight than a dumbbell or bodyweight version.

exercises.name: Glute Bridge
steps: Lying on the floor with your knees bent.
Drive your hips up by squeezing your glutes until your body forms a straight line from shoulders to knees.
The floor-based, bodyweight-friendly version of a hip thrust.

exercises.name: Hip Abduction Machine
steps: Seated on the machine.
Push your knees outward against the pad resistance.
Focusing on your outer glutes rather than jerking the weight with momentum.

exercises.name: Hip Adduction Machine
steps: Seated on the machine.
Squeeze your knees inward against the pad resistance.
Targeting your inner thighs with a slow, controlled motion.

exercises.name: Calf Raise
steps: Standing with the balls of your feet on a raised edge, rise as high onto your toes as possible.
Pause.
Lower your heels below the step for a full stretch.
Avoid bouncing at the bottom.

exercises.name: Seated Calf Raise
steps: Seated with weight across your knees.
Raise your heels by pressing through the balls of your feet.
The seated position emphasizes a different part of the calf than a standing raise.

exercises.name: Sissy Squat
steps: Rising onto your toes.
Lean back and bend your knees while keeping your hips extended and body in a straight line.
Lowering as far as balance and strength allow.
An advanced, quad-isolation squat variation.

exercises.name: High-Bar Back Squat
steps: A back squat with the bar high on the traps and a more upright torso.
Biases the quads and keeps the knees tracking over the toes; descend to at least parallel and drive up.

exercises.name: Low-Bar Back Squat
steps: A back squat with the bar lower across the rear delts and more forward hip lean.
Lets you lift heavier and shares load with the glutes and hamstrings; keep the back flat.

exercises.name: Smith Machine Squat
steps: A squat on the Smith machine's guided bar.
The fixed path removes balance so you can push the quads hard; place the feet slightly forward and descend to at least parallel.

exercises.name: Pause Squat
steps: A back or front squat with a 2–3 second pause at the bottom.
The dead stop kills the bounce and builds strength and control out of the hole; stay tight through the pause.

exercises.name: Tempo Squat
steps: A squat with a deliberately slow descent (e.g. 3–4 seconds down).
The extended time under tension builds control and muscle; keep the same rigid brace the whole rep.

exercises.name: Safety Bar Squat
steps: A squat using a padded safety-squat bar that sits on the shoulders with handles in front.
Easier on the shoulders and biases the upper back and quads; brace hard and stay upright.

exercises.name: Belt Squat
steps: A squat with the load hanging from a hip belt instead of on your back.
Spares the spine while training the quads and glutes hard; great for high volume with no back fatigue.

exercises.name: Landmine Squat
steps: Hold the end of a landmine barbell at your chest and squat.
The arc keeps you upright and is very knee- and back-friendly; a great squat entry point or high-rep finisher.

exercises.name: Heels-Elevated Goblet Squat
steps: A goblet squat with the heels raised on plates or a wedge.
The elevation lets you sit deeper and drives more quad activation; keep the torso tall and the dumbbell at your chest.

exercises.name: Cyclist Squat
steps: A heels-elevated, narrow-stance squat that keeps the torso vertical to maximize quad tension.
Sit straight down over your midfoot; a favorite for building teardrop quad sweep.

exercises.name: Single-Leg Leg Press
steps: A leg press performed one leg at a time.
Isolates each quad and glute, evens out imbalances, and reduces lower-back involvement; press through the whole foot and control the descent.

exercises.name: Reverse Hack Squat
steps: Face into the hack-squat machine (chest against the pad) and squat.
The reversed position biases the glutes and hamstrings while sparing the lower back; drive through the heels.

exercises.name: Machine Squat
steps: A guided squat machine with a shoulder or hip pad.
The fixed path lets beginners and high-rep sets load the quads and glutes safely with no balance demand.

exercises.name: Wall Sit
steps: Slide down a wall until your thighs are parallel to the floor and hold, knees over ankles.
An isometric quad-burner; brace the core.
Keep the back flat on the wall, and hold for time.

exercises.name: Split Squat
steps: A stationary lunge: one foot forward, one back.
Lower straight down until the back knee nears the floor.
Drive up.
Builds single-leg strength; keep the front knee tracking the toe.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Bulgarian Split Squat
steps: A rear-foot-elevated split squat holding dumbbells.
The back foot on a bench forces the front leg to do the work, hammering the quad and glute; keep the torso tall and descend under control.

exercises.name: Deficit Reverse Lunge
steps: A reverse lunge stepping back off a raised platform so the front leg works through extra range.
Deepens the glute and quad stretch; keep the front knee stable and drive back up.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Walking Lunge
steps: Walk forward lunging with a dumbbell in each hand, alternating legs.
A big unilateral quad and glute builder; take a controlled step.
Keep the torso tall.
Drive through the front heel.

exercises.name: Barbell Walking Lunge
steps: Walking lunges with a barbell on your back.
The heavier load builds serious single-leg strength; step under control.
Keep the chest up, and don't let the front knee cave in.

exercises.name: Forward Lunge
steps: Step forward into a lunge until both knees hit ~90°.
Push back to standing.
Trains the quads and glutes; keep the torso upright and the front knee tracking over the foot.

exercises.name: Lateral Lunge
steps: Step out wide to one side and sit back into that hip while the other leg stays straight.
Trains the quads, glutes, and adductors through a side plane; keep the chest up and push back to center.

exercises.name: Curtsy Lunge
steps: Step one leg back and across behind the other into a curtsy.
Return.
The crossover angle targets the glute medius and outer glute; keep the hips square and control the descent.

exercises.name: Front-Foot-Elevated Split Squat
steps: A split squat with the front foot on a small plate or step.
The elevation increases the range and biases the glute and hamstring; keep the torso upright and descend under control.

exercises.name: Standing Leg Curl
steps: Curl one heel toward your glute against a machine pad while standing.
Isolates each hamstring individually; squeeze at the top and lower slowly without swinging the leg.

exercises.name: Single-Leg Lying Leg Curl
steps: A lying leg curl done one leg at a time to even out hamstring imbalances.
Curl the heel toward the glute.
Squeeze, and control the eccentric; keep the hips pinned to the pad.

exercises.name: Swiss Ball Leg Curl
steps: Lying on your back with heels on a stability ball.
Lift the hips and curl the ball toward you.
A bodyweight hamstring and glute move; keep the hips high and control the roll-out.

exercises.name: Slider Leg Curl
steps: Lying on your back with heels on sliders (or towels on a smooth floor), bridge the hips and pull the heels toward you.
A tough eccentric hamstring builder; keep the hips lifted.

exercises.name: Banded Leg Curl
steps: Anchor a band at your ankle and curl the heel toward your glute against its tension.
A joint-friendly hamstring isolation you can do anywhere; squeeze at the top and resist the return.

exercises.name: Glute-Ham Raise
steps: On a GHD.
Lower your torso forward from the knees under hamstring control.
Pull back up.
One of the best posterior-chain builders; keep the hips extended and the movement smooth.

exercises.name: Razor Curl
steps: A GHD or bench hamstring curl where the hips flex slightly as you rise.
Keeping constant tension.
A brutal hamstring finisher; control the lowering phase and don't rush.

exercises.name: Kettlebell Romanian Deadlift
steps: A hip-hinge RDL holding a kettlebell (or two).
Push the hips back with a flat back until you feel the hamstring stretch.
Squeeze the glutes to stand; keep the weight close.

exercises.name: B-Stance Romanian Deadlift
steps: An RDL with one foot staggered slightly back as a kickstand, loading mostly the front leg.
A bridge between two-leg and single-leg hinges; hinge back and feel the working hamstring.

exercises.name: Cable Pull-Through
steps: Face away from a low cable, straddle the rope.
Hinge.
Push the hips back then snap them forward.
Squeezing the glutes.
A hip-hinge pattern with constant glute tension.

exercises.name: Seated Good Morning
steps: Seated with a barbell on your back.
Hinge your torso forward from the hips and return.
Trains the lower back and hamstrings with the legs taken out; keep a flat, braced spine.

exercises.name: Single-Leg Hip Thrust
steps: A hip thrust driving through one foot with the other leg raised.
The single-leg load hammers each glute and exposes imbalances; squeeze hard at the top and keep the hips level.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Hip Thrust
steps: A hip thrust with a dumbbell across the hips, shoulders on a bench.
Drive through the heels to full hip extension and squeeze the glutes at the top; a great at-home glute builder.

exercises.name: Machine Hip Thrust
steps: A dedicated hip-thrust machine with a padded lap bar.
The fixed path lets you load the glutes heavy and safely; drive to full extension and pause with a hard glute squeeze.

exercises.name: Frog Pump
steps: Lying on your back with the soles of your feet together and knees splayed, pump the hips up and squeeze the glutes.
The frog position biases the glutes over the hamstrings; go for reps.

exercises.name: Banded Glute Bridge
steps: A glute bridge with a mini-band above the knees, pushing the knees out as you lift.
The band adds glute-medius activation; squeeze the glutes hard at the top of each rep.

exercises.name: B-Stance Hip Thrust
steps: A hip thrust with one foot staggered as a kickstand so most of the load goes through the front leg.
A way to overload each glute without full single-leg balance; squeeze at the top.

exercises.name: Cable Glute Kickback
steps: With an ankle strap on a low cable.
Drive one leg straight back and up.
Squeezing the glute.
Isolates each glute through a controlled range; keep the torso still and avoid arching the back.

exercises.name: Cable Hip Abduction
steps: With an ankle strap on a low cable.
Lift one leg out to the side against the cable.
Targets the glute medius; keep the torso upright and control the return without swinging.

exercises.name: Banded Lateral Walk
steps: With a mini-band around the knees or ankles.
Step sideways in a half-squat.
Keeping tension the whole time.
A glute-medius activator; stay low and don't let the knees cave in.

exercises.name: Banded Monster Walk
steps: With a band around the legs.
Step diagonally forward and out in a half-squat.
Fires up the glutes and hips; keep constant band tension and the knees pushed out throughout.

exercises.name: Standing Glute Kickback (Machine)
steps: On a glute-kickback machine.
Drive one foot back against the pad to full hip extension.
Isolates each glute with a fixed path; squeeze at the top and control the return.

exercises.name: Step-Through Lunge
steps: Lunge forward.
Without stopping step the same leg straight back into a reverse lunge.
The continuous front-and-back motion torches the working quad and glute; keep the torso tall.

exercises.name: Kettlebell Sumo Deadlift
steps: A wide-stance deadlift lifting a kettlebell between the legs.
The sumo stance biases the glutes, inner thighs, and quads; push the hips forward to stand and keep the back flat.

exercises.name: Standing Calf Raise (Machine)
steps: On a standing calf machine with the shoulders under the pads, rise onto the balls of your feet.
Pause at the top.
Lower into a full stretch.
Train the full range for calf growth.

exercises.name: Smith Machine Calf Raise
steps: A standing calf raise with the bar on your shoulders in a Smith machine and toes on a plate.
The guided bar lets you load heavy; get a deep stretch at the bottom and a hard squeeze up top.

exercises.name: Leg Press Calf Raise
steps: On the leg press with only the balls of your feet on the platform.
Press through the toes to full ankle extension and lower into a stretch.
A safe way to load the calves heavy.

exercises.name: Single-Leg Calf Raise
steps: A calf raise on one foot.
Holding a dumbbell for load.
The single-leg version exposes and fixes side-to-side imbalances; get a full stretch at the bottom and rise all the way up.

exercises.name: Donkey Calf Raise
steps: Hinge at the hips with weight on your lower back or a machine pad and raise the heels.
The bent-over position gives the calves a huge stretch; pause at the top and bottom.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Calf Raise
steps: A standing calf raise holding a dumbbell, one leg or two, with the toes on a plate for range.
Rise onto the balls of the feet.
Squeeze the calves.
Lower into a full stretch.

exercises.name: Tibialis Raise
steps: With your back to a wall and heels forward.
Raise your toes toward your shins against bodyweight or a band.
Strengthens the shin muscle for knee health and jump/sprint resilience.

exercises.name: Seated Dumbbell Calf Raise
steps: Seated with a dumbbell on your knees and toes on a plate.
Raise the heels to work the soleus (deep calf).
The bent-knee position targets the lower calf; use a slow, full range.

exercises.name: Calf Press (Leg Press)
steps: Push the leg-press platform with the balls of your feet only, extending the ankles fully.
A heavy, back-safe calf builder; pause at full extension and lower into a deep stretch.

exercises.name: Copenhagen Plank
steps: A side plank with the top leg braced on a bench and the bottom leg lifting toward it.
One of the best adductor (inner-thigh) strengtheners; keep the hips high and hold or do reps.

exercises.name: Jefferson Squat
steps: Straddle a barbell and lift it with a staggered stance and mixed grip.
An old-school squat/deadlift hybrid that trains the legs and core from an unusual angle; keep the back flat.

exercises.name: Anderson Squat
steps: A squat starting from a dead stop with the bar on the rack's pins at the bottom.
Removes the stretch reflex to build raw strength out of the hole; drive up from a full stop.

exercises.name: Pin Squat
steps: A squat descending to safety pins set at a target depth.
Pausing on them each rep.
Reinforces consistent depth and builds bottom-end strength; stay braced through the dead stop.

exercises.name: Goblet Box Squat
steps: A goblet squat sitting back to a box or bench each rep.
The box teaches depth and hip loading and is very beginner-friendly; touch lightly and drive up without collapsing.

exercises.name: Eccentric Nordic Curl
steps: Kneeling with the ankles anchored.
Lower your torso forward as slowly as possible under hamstring control.
Push off the floor to reset.
A hamstring-strength and injury-prevention staple.

exercises.name: Reverse Nordic Curl
steps: Kneeling upright.
Lean your torso back from the knees under control while keeping the hips extended.
Return.
A big quad and knee-strength builder; only go as far as you can control.

exercises.name: Sumo Goblet Squat
steps: A goblet squat with a wide stance and toes turned out.
Holding a dumbbell or kettlebell at the chest.
The sumo stance biases the glutes and inner thighs; sit straight down and drive up tall.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Reverse Lunge
steps: A reverse lunge holding a dumbbell in each hand.
Stepping back is easier on the knees than stepping forward; drive through the front heel to stand.

exercises.name: Barbell Reverse Lunge
steps: A reverse lunge with a barbell on the upper back.
Lets you load the pattern heavily; keep the torso tall and the front shin vertical.

exercises.name: Overhead Lunge
steps: A walking or reverse lunge with a barbell or plate locked out overhead.
The overhead load turns it into a full-body stability test; keep the ribs down and arms locked.

exercises.name: Jumping Lunge
steps: From a split stance, jump and switch legs in the air, landing softly in a lunge.
A quad and conditioning burner; land quietly and keep the front knee tracking over the toes.

exercises.name: Deficit Forward Lunge
steps: A forward lunge stepping onto a low platform so the back knee travels below foot level.
The extra range loads the glutes and hamstrings harder; control the descent.

exercises.name: Landmine Reverse Lunge
steps: A reverse lunge holding the end of a landmine barbell at the chest.
The bar's arc helps you stay upright, making it a great heavy lunge for beginners.

exercises.name: Slider Reverse Lunge
steps: A reverse lunge sliding the back foot along the floor on a towel or slider.
The constant tension makes even bodyweight sets hard; move slowly in both directions.

exercises.name: Calf Raise on Step
steps: A standing calf raise with the toes on a step so the heels can drop below the platform.
The deeper stretch at the bottom is where most of the growth comes from.

exercises.name: Barbell Calf Raise
steps: A standing calf raise with a barbell on the upper back.
Lets you load heavier than dumbbells allow; pause at the top of every rep.

exercises.name: Hack Squat Calf Raise
steps: A calf raise done standing on the footplate of a hack squat machine.
The fixed back support means the calves take everything; press through the balls of the feet.

exercises.name: Bent-Knee Calf Raise
steps: A calf raise with the knees softly bent throughout, biasing the soleus underneath the calf.
Use higher reps -- the soleus responds to volume.

exercises.name: Banded Calf Raise
steps: A calf raise standing on a band with the handles held at the shoulders.
A simple loaded calf option at home; squeeze hard at the top.

exercises.name: Narrow-Stance Leg Press
steps: A leg press with the feet close together, low on the platform.
Biases the quads and outer thigh; keep the knees tracking over the toes.

exercises.name: Wide-Stance Leg Press
steps: A leg press with the feet set wide and toes turned slightly out.
Brings the adductors and glutes in alongside the quads.

exercises.name: High-Foot Leg Press
steps: A leg press with the feet high on the platform.
Shifts the load toward the glutes and hamstrings; don't let the low back round at the bottom.

exercises.name: Low-Foot Leg Press
steps: A leg press with the feet low on the platform.
A pure quad emphasis; keep the heels down and stop short of lockout.

exercises.name: Horizontal Leg Press
steps: A seated leg press where you push the platform straight out in front of you.
Easier on the low back than the 45-degree sled; control the return.

exercises.name: Vertical Leg Press
steps: A leg press pushing the platform straight up while lying flat on your back.
Very demanding on the hips and low back -- keep the range moderate and the weight sensible.

exercises.name: Paused Leg Press
steps: A leg press held for two seconds at the bottom before pressing back up.
The pause removes the bounce and builds strength out of the deep position.

exercises.name: Feet-Together Leg Press
steps: A leg press with the feet touching in the middle of the platform.
Hits the outer quad sweep; keep the knees from caving in.

exercises.name: Banded Leg Press
steps: A leg press with bands added to the sled for accommodating resistance.
Resistance rises as you extend, so the lockout is the hardest part.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Step-Up
steps: A step-up onto a box holding a dumbbell in each hand.
Drive through the whole front foot and avoid pushing off the back leg.

exercises.name: Barbell Step-Up
steps: A step-up with a barbell on the upper back.
Heavy and demanding on balance; start with a low box and keep the torso tall.

exercises.name: Lateral Step-Up
steps: A step-up done sideways onto the box, leading with the outside leg.
Trains the glute medius and knee stability in a plane most training ignores.

exercises.name: High Box Step-Up
steps: A step-up onto a box at or above knee height.
The deep start position loads the glutes hard; go slow and don't push off the trailing foot.

exercises.name: Kettlebell Step-Up
steps: A step-up with a kettlebell held in the rack position at the shoulder.
The front-loaded position makes the core work to keep you upright.

exercises.name: Step-Up with Knee Drive
steps: A step-up finished by driving the trailing knee up to hip height.
Adds a balance and hip-flexor challenge; pause at the top of each rep.

exercises.name: Slow-Tempo Step-Up
steps: A step-up taking three seconds up and three seconds down.
The slow eccentric is where the quad and glute growth is; no bouncing off the floor.

exercises.name: Crossover Step-Up
steps: Standing beside a box, cross the far leg over and step up onto it.
A strong glute medius builder; keep the hips level throughout.

exercises.name: Bench Step-Up
steps: A step-up onto a flat bench, the most common gym platform for the movement.
Check the bench is stable, and step down under control rather than dropping.

exercises.name: Banded Step-Up
steps: A step-up standing on a band with the handles held at the shoulders.
Resistance increases as you extend the hip, so the top of the rep is hardest.

exercises.name: Deficit Step-Down
steps: Standing on a box, lower one foot slowly to tap the floor and press back up.
An eccentric-focused single-leg builder that's excellent for knee health.

exercises.name: Smith Machine Hip Thrust
steps: A hip thrust with the bar on a Smith machine, so the path is fixed and setup is quick.
Drive through the heels and squeeze the glutes hard at the top.

exercises.name: Banded Hip Thrust
steps: A hip thrust with a band over the hips or around the knees.
Tension peaks at lockout, exactly where the glutes work hardest.

exercises.name: Feet-Elevated Hip Thrust
steps: A hip thrust with the feet raised on a low box or plates.
The longer range shifts more work to the hamstrings alongside the glutes.

exercises.name: Paused Hip Thrust
steps: A hip thrust held for two to three seconds at full lockout each rep.
The pause forces a real glute contraction instead of a bounce.

exercises.name: Bodyweight Hip Thrust
steps: A shoulders-on-bench hip thrust with no external load.
A great way to learn the pattern and to warm the glutes up before heavy work.

exercises.name: Kettlebell Hip Thrust
steps: A hip thrust with a kettlebell resting across the hips.
Easier to set up solo than a barbell; keep the chin tucked and ribs down.

exercises.name: Cable Hip Thrust
steps: A hip thrust driven against a low cable attached at the hips.
The cable's constant tension makes lockout the hardest point of every rep.

exercises.name: Barbell Glute Bridge
steps: A glute bridge from the floor with a barbell across the hips.
Shorter range than a hip thrust but easy to load heavy; squeeze at the top.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Glute Bridge
steps: A floor glute bridge with a dumbbell held across the hips.
A simple loaded glute option that needs no bench.

exercises.name: Feet-Elevated Glute Bridge
steps: A glute bridge with the heels up on a step or bench.
Increases the hamstring share of the work; keep the ribs down.

exercises.name: Glute Bridge March
steps: Hold the top of a glute bridge and lift one knee at a time toward your chest.
The single-leg support turns it into an anti-rotation core drill too.

exercises.name: Frog Glute Bridge
steps: A glute bridge with the soles of the feet together and knees splayed out.
The externally rotated hips bias the upper glutes; squeeze hard for a full second.

exercises.name: Banded Glute Kickback
steps: A kneeling or standing kickback against a band looped round the ankle.
Drive the heel straight back and stop when the low back wants to arch.

exercises.name: Quadruped Glute Kickback
steps: On hands and knees, press one heel toward the ceiling with the knee bent at 90 degrees.
Keep the hips square and the movement small and controlled.

exercises.name: Sliding Hamstring Curl
steps: Lying on your back with the heels on sliders, bridge up and pull the heels toward the hips.
A punishing bodyweight hamstring curl; keep the hips high throughout.

exercises.name: Banded Hamstring Curl
steps: A lying leg curl against a band anchored behind you.
A joint-friendly way to train the hamstrings without a machine.

exercises.name: Single-Leg Stability Ball Hamstring Curl
steps: A stability ball hamstring curl done one leg at a time.
Roughly doubles the load per leg and adds a serious stability demand.

exercises.name: Razor Hamstring Curl
steps: A kneeling hamstring curl with the hips flexing back and then extending as you lower and rise.
A slightly more forgiving progression toward the Nordic curl.

exercises.name: Standing Hamstring Curl (Machine)
steps: A one-leg-at-a-time curl on a standing leg-curl machine.
Lets each hamstring work independently; keep the hips pressed into the pad.

exercises.name: Eccentric Nordic Hamstring Curl
steps: A Nordic curl lowering as slowly as possible, then pushing back up with the hands.
The gold-standard hamstring injury-prevention exercise; three to five reps is plenty.

exercises.name: Banded Hip Abduction
steps: Seated or standing with a band above the knees, press the knees apart against the band.
A simple glute medius burner; hold each rep for a beat.

exercises.name: Side-Lying Hip Abduction
steps: Lying on your side, raise the top leg toward the ceiling with the toes pointing forward.
Keep the hips stacked so the glute does the work, not the hip flexor.

exercises.name: Standing Cable Hip Abduction
steps: With a cuff on the ankle, sweep the leg out to the side against a low cable.
Trains the glute medius standing, the way it actually works when you walk.

exercises.name: Banded Hip Adduction
steps: With a band anchored to the side and looped round the ankle, pull the leg in across the body.
Strengthens the inner thigh, which most programs never train directly.

exercises.name: Side-Lying Hip Adduction
steps: Lying on your side with the top leg crossed in front, raise the bottom leg off the floor.
A simple bodyweight adductor exercise; move slowly and keep the leg straight.

exercises.name: Copenhagen Adduction
steps: A side plank with the top leg on a bench, lifting the bottom leg up to meet it.
One of the strongest groin-injury-prevention exercises there is; start with the knee on the bench.

exercises.name: Standing Hip Adduction (Machine)
steps: A standing adduction machine, sweeping one leg in across the body.
Keep the torso upright and control the return; don't let the leg snap back.

exercises.name: Plank
steps: Hold a straight line from your head to your heels, supported on your forearms and toes.
Keeping your hips level.
Squeeze your glutes and abs so your lower back doesn't sag.

exercises.name: Side Plank
steps: Balanced on one forearm and the side of one foot.
Keep your body in a straight line from head to feet without letting your hips drop toward the floor.

exercises.name: Crunch
steps: Lying on your back with knees bent.
Curl your shoulders up off the floor using your abs.
Keeping your lower back pressed down.
Avoid pulling on your neck with your hands.

exercises.name: Bicycle Crunch
steps: Lying on your back, hands behind your head.
Bring one elbow toward the opposite knee while extending the other leg out.
Switch sides in a smooth pedaling motion.
Twist from your ribs, not by yanking on your neck.

exercises.name: Cable Crunch
steps: Kneeling below a high cable.
Curl your torso down by rounding your spine and bringing your elbows toward your knees.
Using your abs rather than pulling with your arms.

exercises.name: Sit-Up
steps: Lying on your back with knees bent and feet anchored.
Curl your entire torso up until you're sitting upright.
Lower back down under control.

exercises.name: V-Up
steps: Lying flat, simultaneously raise your straight legs and straight arms to meet in a V-shape above your hips.
Lower back down under control.
A harder, full-range alternative to a standard sit-up.

exercises.name: Hanging Leg Raise
steps: Hanging from a bar.
Raise your legs (bent or straight) up toward your chest using your abs, avoiding swinging your body to generate momentum.
Lower back down slowly rather than dropping your legs.

exercises.name: Ab Wheel Rollout
steps: Kneeling and gripping the wheel, roll it forward as far as you can while keeping your core braced and back flat.
Pull back to the start using your abs.
Stop before your lower back starts to sag.

exercises.name: Cable Woodchopper
steps: Pull a cable diagonally across your body, from high to low or low to high.
Rotating through your torso while keeping your hips relatively stable.
Mimics a chopping motion.
Targeting your obliques.

exercises.name: Russian Twist
steps: Seated with your torso leaned back and feet either on the floor or lifted.
Rotate a weight from side to side, touching it near the floor on each side.
Control the rotation rather than using momentum to fling it.

exercises.name: Dead Bug
steps: Lying on your back with arms and legs in the air, slowly extend one arm and the opposite leg toward the floor while keeping your lower back pressed flat.
Return and switch sides.

exercises.name: Mountain Climber
steps: In a push-up position.
Drive your knees toward your chest one at a time in a running motion.
Keeping your hips low and core braced rather than bouncing your hips up and down.

exercises.name: Hanging Knee Raise
steps: Hang from a bar and raise your knees toward your chest, curling the pelvis up rather than just swinging the legs.
Control the lower and don't let momentum kip you; a lower-ab staple.

exercises.name: Hanging Windshield Wiper
steps: Hang from a bar.
Raise the legs.
Sweep them side to side like wipers.
An advanced obliques and lower-ab move; keep the movement controlled and the shoulders active.

exercises.name: Toes-to-Bar
steps: Hang from a bar and raise your straight legs until your toes touch it.
A full-range lower-ab and hip-flexor move; control the descent and avoid excessive swinging.

exercises.name: Captain's Chair Leg Raise
steps: In a captain's-chair station with forearms on the pads.
Raise your knees or straight legs toward your chest.
The back support isolates the abs; curl the pelvis and lower slowly.

exercises.name: Lying Leg Raise
steps: Lying flat.
Raise your straight legs to vertical then lower them without letting the lower back arch off the floor.
A lower-ab builder; press the low back down throughout.

exercises.name: Reverse Crunch
steps: Lying on your back.
Curl your knees and hips up toward your chest, lifting the tailbone off the floor.
Targets the lower abs; use control, not momentum, and don't yank with the legs.

exercises.name: Weighted Crunch
steps: A crunch holding a plate or dumbbell on your chest.
The added load builds the upper abs; curl the ribcage toward the pelvis and squeeze.
Lower under control.

exercises.name: Decline Sit-Up
steps: A full sit-up on a decline bench with feet anchored.
The angle increases the range and difficulty; curl up smoothly and lower with control.
Adding a plate to progress.

exercises.name: Low-to-High Cable Chop
steps: From a low pulley.
Pull the handle diagonally up and across your body to the opposite shoulder.
Rotating through the core.
A standing obliques and anti-rotation builder; keep the arms long.

exercises.name: High-to-Low Cable Chop
steps: From a high pulley.
Pull the handle diagonally down and across to the opposite hip.
Rotating through the trunk.
Trains the obliques through a chopping pattern; control the return.

exercises.name: Landmine Rotation
steps: Hold the end of a landmine barbell at arm's length and arc it side to side across your body.
Rotating through the hips and core.
A powerful rotational obliques move; keep the arms straight.

exercises.name: Standing Cable Crunch
steps: Facing a high pulley with a rope behind your head, crunch your ribcage down toward your pelvis.
The cable keeps constant tension on the abs; round the spine, don't just hinge at the hips.

exercises.name: Weighted Plank
steps: A forearm plank with a plate on your back for added load.
Brace the whole body in a straight line and hold for time; the extra weight builds serious core stiffness.

exercises.name: Plank Shoulder Tap
steps: In a high plank, tap each hand to the opposite shoulder while keeping the hips completely still.
The anti-rotation demand hits the deep core; move slowly and don't let the hips sway.

exercises.name: RKC Plank
steps: A forearm plank cranked to maximum tension: squeeze the glutes, quads, and abs as hard as possible and hold.
A short, intense full-body brace; 10–20 seconds is plenty.

exercises.name: Long-Lever Plank
steps: A forearm plank with the elbows placed further forward than usual, lengthening the lever.
Dramatically increases the ab demand; keep the hips level and hold only as long as form holds.

exercises.name: Side Plank with Reach-Through
steps: From a side plank.
Rotate and thread the top arm under your body.
Reach it back to the sky.
Trains the obliques dynamically; keep the hips high and the motion controlled.

exercises.name: Star Plank
steps: A side plank with the top arm and top leg both raised into a star shape.
A tough obliques and hip-stability hold; keep the body in one line and the hips lifted.

exercises.name: Hollow Body Hold
steps: Lying on your back.
Press the low back into the floor and lift the shoulders and legs into a shallow 'banana' shape.
A foundational core-tension hold; keep the ribs down and hold for time.

exercises.name: Hollow Body Rock
steps: From a hollow-body position, rock gently back and forth as one rigid piece.
The rocking adds a dynamic challenge to the core brace; keep the low back glued down throughout.

exercises.name: Flutter Kick
steps: Lying on your back with legs straight and slightly raised, alternately kick them up and down in small, fast scissoring motions.
A lower-ab and hip-flexor burner; keep the low back pressed down.

exercises.name: Scissor Kick
steps: Lying on your back with legs raised, cross them over and under each other in a scissoring motion.
Targets the lower abs and inner thighs; keep the low back flat and the movement controlled.

exercises.name: Toe Touch Crunch
steps: Lying on your back with legs straight up.
Reach your hands toward your toes by crunching the upper abs.
A strict upper-ab move; lift the shoulder blades off the floor and lower slowly.

exercises.name: Heel Tap
steps: Lying with knees bent and shoulders slightly raised, crunch side to side to tap each heel with the same-side hand.
A simple oblique burner; keep the shoulders off the floor throughout.

exercises.name: Medicine Ball Russian Twist
steps: Seated and leaning back with the feet up.
Rotate a medicine ball from hip to hip, following it with your eyes.
A loaded rotational obliques move; keep the chest up and move under control.

exercises.name: Standing Ab Wheel Rollout
steps: From a standing bent-over position, roll an ab wheel out until your body is nearly horizontal.
Pull back.
The standing version is an advanced anti-extension challenge; keep the core braced.

exercises.name: Stir-the-Pot
steps: In a plank with forearms on a stability ball, draw small circles with the forearms.
The moving base forces the deep core to fight rotation and extension; keep the hips and spine still.

exercises.name: L-Sit Hold
steps: Supported on parallettes or the floor.
Lift your body with straight legs held out in front to form an 'L' and hold.
A serious core and hip-flexor isometric; start with tucked knees to build up.

exercises.name: Dragon Flag
steps: Lying on a bench gripping behind your head.
Raise your whole body to near-vertical then lower it straight and rigid.
A legendary advanced core move; keep the body in one line and control the descent.

exercises.name: Half-Kneeling Pallof Press
steps: In a half-kneeling stance beside a cable.
Press the handle straight out and resist its pull toward the machine.
An anti-rotation core exercise; keep the hips square and don't let the torso twist.

exercises.name: Hanging Oblique Raise
steps: Hang from a bar and raise your knees up and out to one side, then the other.
The diagonal curl targets the obliques and lower abs; control the swing and keep the shoulders active.

exercises.name: Machine Crunch
steps: A seated ab crunch machine with the chest pad loaded by a weight stack.
The easiest way to progressively overload the abs; curl the ribs toward the hips.

exercises.name: Decline Crunch
steps: A crunch on a decline bench with the feet anchored.
The angle adds resistance at the top of the crunch; don't pull on your neck.

exercises.name: Stability Ball Crunch
steps: A crunch lying back over a stability ball so the spine can extend past flat.
The extra range makes it far more effective than a floor crunch.

exercises.name: Oblique Crunch
steps: A crunch driving the elbow toward the opposite knee, or crunching sideways with the knees dropped.
Hits the obliques; hold the top for a beat each rep.

exercises.name: Frog Crunch
steps: A crunch with the soles of the feet together and knees splayed out.
Takes the hip flexors out of the movement so the abs do everything.

exercises.name: Butterfly Crunch
steps: A crunch with the legs in a butterfly position and arms reaching overhead.
The long lever makes a bodyweight crunch genuinely hard.

exercises.name: Long-Arm Crunch
steps: A crunch with the arms held straight overhead beside the ears throughout.
The extended arms lengthen the lever and increase the ab demand.

exercises.name: Double Crunch
steps: Crunch the shoulders and the knees toward each other at the same time.
Trains the upper and lower abs in one movement; exhale hard at the top.

exercises.name: Weighted Sit-Up
steps: A sit-up holding a plate or dumbbell against the chest.
The simplest way to make sit-ups a strength exercise rather than an endurance one.

exercises.name: Butterfly Sit-Up
steps: A sit-up with the soles of the feet together and knees out.
The open hips stop the hip flexors taking over; reach past the feet at the top.

exercises.name: V Sit-Up
steps: From lying flat, lift the legs and torso together to meet in a V shape.
Hits the whole front of the core; lower both halves slowly.

exercises.name: Stability Ball Sit-Up
steps: A full sit-up performed lying back over a stability ball.
The extended range makes it a much fuller ab contraction than a floor sit-up.

exercises.name: Twisting Sit-Up
steps: A sit-up rotating toward one knee at the top, alternating sides.
Brings the obliques into a standard sit-up.

exercises.name: Anchored Sit-Up
steps: A sit-up with the feet hooked under a bar or held down.
Lets you sit up against heavier loads, at the cost of more hip flexor involvement.

exercises.name: Medicine Ball Sit-Up Throw
steps: Sit up and throw a medicine ball to a partner or wall at the top of each rep.
Adds explosive power to the pattern; catch it and lower under control.

exercises.name: Hanging Straight-Leg Raise
steps: A hanging leg raise with the knees locked straight throughout.
Far harder than the bent-knee version; stop swinging before starting the next rep.

exercises.name: Weighted Hanging Leg Raise
steps: A hanging leg raise with a dumbbell held between the feet.
The most direct way to overload the lower abs; keep the movement strict.

exercises.name: Parallel Bar Leg Raise
steps: A leg raise supported on parallel bars or a captain's chair with the elbows down.
Removes the grip limitation so the abs are the only thing that fails.

exercises.name: Incline Bench Leg Raise
steps: A leg raise lying on a decline bench gripping the top for support.
The angle keeps the abs loaded even at the bottom of each rep.

exercises.name: Roman Chair Leg Raise
steps: A leg raise from a Roman chair with the back supported.
A stable position that lets you focus purely on curling the pelvis up.

exercises.name: Side-Lying Leg Raise
steps: Lying on your side, raise both legs together off the floor.
A tough oblique and hip exercise; keep the shoulders stacked.

exercises.name: Banded Leg Raise
steps: A lying leg raise against a band anchored behind your head and looped round the feet.
Adds resistance to a bodyweight staple; lower slowly against the band.

exercises.name: Bench Leg Raise
steps: A lying leg raise on a flat bench, gripping the bench behind your head with the hips just off the edge.
The extra range below the bench loads the lower abs harder than the floor.

exercises.name: Plank Jack
steps: In a plank, jump the feet wide and back together while keeping the hips still.
Adds a conditioning element to a core hold; don't let the hips bounce.

exercises.name: Plank to Push-Up
steps: Move from a forearm plank up to a high plank one arm at a time, then back down.
An anti-rotation core exercise with a tricep and shoulder bonus.

exercises.name: Reverse Plank
steps: Sit with the legs straight and hands behind you, then lift the hips into a straight line facing up.
Trains the posterior chain and counteracts a day of sitting.

exercises.name: Plank with Leg Lift
steps: A forearm plank raising one leg a few inches off the floor at a time.
Taking away a base of support forces the deep core to fight rotation.

exercises.name: Single-Arm Plank
steps: A plank holding one arm off the floor, extended or tucked behind the back.
A serious anti-rotation challenge; keep the hips completely level.

exercises.name: Plank Reach-Out
steps: From a forearm plank, reach one arm straight out in front and hold before swapping.
The long lever makes the abs work far harder than a standard plank.

exercises.name: Cable Torso Twist
steps: Standing side-on to a cable at chest height, rotate the handle across the body with straight arms.
A pure rotational obliques exercise; turn from the ribcage, not the arms.

exercises.name: Standing Band Twist
steps: The same rotation against a band anchored at chest height.
Keep the hips facing forward so the rotation comes from the trunk.

exercises.name: Plank Hip Twist
steps: In a forearm plank, rotate the hips to tap each side toward the floor.
Trains the obliques dynamically; move slowly and keep the shoulders square.

exercises.name: Hanging Knee Twist
steps: Hanging from a bar, raise the knees and rotate them to one side, alternating.
Combines a lower-ab raise with an oblique twist; control the swing.

exercises.name: Weighted Russian Twist
steps: A Russian twist holding a plate or dumbbell, rotating hip to hip.
Keep the chest tall and the feet up; rotate the ribcage rather than swinging the arms.

exercises.name: Seated Barbell Twist
steps: Seated on a bench with a light bar across the shoulders, rotate side to side.
A classic oblique warm-up; keep it light and never force the range.

exercises.name: Half-Kneeling Cable Rotation
steps: A cable rotation from a half-kneeling stance, turning away from the machine.
The locked-down hips mean all the rotation comes from the trunk.

exercises.name: Standing Cable Rotation
steps: A standing cable rotation at chest height, pivoting the back foot as you turn.
The closest gym exercise to the rotation used in throwing and swinging sports.

exercises.name: Kettlebell Swing
steps: Hinge at your hips to swing the kettlebell back between your legs.
Snap your hips forward explosively to drive it up to chest height.
This is a hip-hinge power move, not a shoulder-lifting move.

exercises.name: Farmer's Carry
steps: Hold a heavy weight in each hand and walk for distance or time.
Keeping your shoulders back and core braced.
Simple in concept, but a great full-body grip and stability builder.

exercises.name: Thruster
steps: Combine a front squat with an overhead press.
Squat down.
Use the upward momentum from standing back up to drive the weight straight overhead in one fluid motion.

exercises.name: Burpee
steps: Drop into a squat, kick your feet back into a plank, perform a push-up (optional), jump your feet back to your hands.
Explode upward into a jump.
A full-body conditioning move, so prioritize form over speed as fatigue builds.

exercises.name: Devil Press
steps: A burpee with a dumbbell in each hand: burpee down.
As you stand back up swing both dumbbells from the floor to overhead in one motion (like a two-arm kettlebell swing to snatch).
A brutal full-body HYROX/hybrid conditioning staple.

exercises.name: Clean and Jerk
steps: An advanced Olympic lift: explosively pull the bar from the floor to your shoulders (the clean).
Drive it overhead with a leg-drive dip (the jerk).
This technical lift is best learned from a coach in person before loading it heavily.

exercises.name: Snatch
steps: An advanced Olympic lift that pulls the bar from the floor straight overhead in one continuous motion.
Catching it in a deep squat.
Like the clean and jerk, this is a highly technical movement best learned under direct coaching first.

exercises.name: Wall Ball Shot
steps: Holding a medicine ball at your chest, squat down.
Stand up explosively and throw the ball to a target on the wall above you.
Catching it on the way back down into the next squat.
A HYROX staple that blends leg power with shoulder endurance.

exercises.name: Sled Push
steps: Load a weighted sled and drive it forward across the floor with both hands.
Staying low with your shins angled forward.
Push through your whole foot, not just your toes.
Keep your arms mostly locked out.

exercises.name: Sled Pull
steps: Attach a rope or straps to a loaded sled and pull it toward you hand-over-hand (or walk backward dragging it).
Keep your core braced and your pulls steady rather than jerky.

exercises.name: Box Jump Over
steps: Jump onto a box.
Step or jump down the other side (rather than jumping back off the way you came).
A continuous-conditioning variation of a box jump used in HYROX-style workouts; land soft and reset your balance before the next rep.

exercises.name: Rowing Machine Intervals
steps: Alternate hard, fast rowing efforts with easier recovery pacing on a rowing machine.
Drive with your legs first.
Lean back and pull with your arms, reversing the order on the way back up the slide.

exercises.name: Assault Bike Intervals
steps: Alternate hard, fast sprints with easier recovery pacing on an air/fan bike, pushing and pulling with your arms as well as pedaling.
The fan resistance scales with your effort, so pacing is entirely up to you.

exercises.name: Power Clean
steps: Explosively pull a barbell from the floor and catch it on the front of the shoulders in a partial squat.
A full-body power move; drive with the hips and receive the bar with soft knees.

exercises.name: Hang Clean
steps: A power clean starting from the hang (bar at the hips) rather than the floor.
Teaches the explosive hip drive and catch; snap the hips and pull yourself under the bar.

exercises.name: Power Snatch
steps: Explosively pull a barbell from the floor overhead to a locked-out catch in one motion with a wide grip.
The most explosive full-body lift; drive with the hips and punch the bar up.

exercises.name: Hang Snatch
steps: A power snatch starting from the hang at the hips.
Grooves the fast hip extension and overhead catch without the floor pull; keep the bar close and lock out overhead.

exercises.name: Clean Pull
steps: The pulling portion of a clean without the catch: explosively extend the hips and shrug the bar up to the waist/chest.
Builds power and pulling strength; finish tall on the toes.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Clean and Press
steps: Explosively pull two dumbbells to the shoulders.
Press them overhead.
A full-body strength and conditioning move; drive with the hips on the clean and brace hard on the press.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Snatch
steps: Explosively pull a single dumbbell from between the feet to a locked-out position overhead in one motion.
A full-body power and conditioning staple; alternate arms and drive with the hips.

exercises.name: Kettlebell Clean
steps: Swing a kettlebell up and rotate the hand around it to catch it softly in the rack position at the shoulder.
The foundation of most kettlebell complexes; guide it, don't let it bang the forearm.

exercises.name: Kettlebell Clean and Press
steps: Clean a kettlebell to the shoulder.
Press it overhead.
A full-body strength builder that trains the hips, shoulders, and core in one movement; keep the wrist straight and press strict.

exercises.name: Kettlebell Snatch
steps: Swing a kettlebell overhead in one explosive motion, punching the hand through at the top to catch it softly.
A high-power conditioning move; drive with the hips and control the receive.

exercises.name: Kettlebell Goblet Squat
steps: Hold a kettlebell at your chest by the horns and squat between your knees.
A beginner-friendly, upright squat that hits the quads, glutes, and core; sit deep and drive through the heels.

exercises.name: Man Maker
steps: A brutal combo: renegade rows, a push-up, a clean, and an overhead press with two dumbbells in one sequence.
Full-body strength and conditioning; keep the core braced through every phase.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Thruster
steps: Front-squat two dumbbells at the shoulders.
Drive up and press them overhead in one fluid motion.
A full-body strength-and-cardio move; use the leg drive to launch the press.

exercises.name: Wall Walk
steps: From a push-up on the floor facing away from a wall, walk your feet up the wall and hands in toward it into a handstand.
Reverse.
A full-body shoulder and core builder; move slowly.

exercises.name: Bear Complex
steps: A barbell chain of power clean, front squat.
Push press, back squat, and second push press done unbroken.
A savage full-body conditioning circuit; keep the reps crisp and the core braced.

exercises.name: Barbell Complex
steps: A sequence of barbell lifts (e.g. row, clean, front squat.
Press, back squat) done back-to-back without setting the bar down.
Builds strength-endurance; pick a weight the weakest lift can handle.

exercises.name: Sandbag Get-Up
steps: Hug a sandbag to your chest and stand up from the floor and back down, repeatedly.
A rugged full-body and core builder that mimics real-world lifting; keep the bag tight and the back flat.

exercises.name: American Kettlebell Swing
steps: A kettlebell swing driven all the way overhead rather than to chest height.
More shoulder demand; only add the overhead finish once your hinge is solid.

exercises.name: Single-Arm Kettlebell Swing
steps: A kettlebell swing with one hand, switching hands at the top or between sets.
Adds a strong anti-rotation core demand; keep the shoulder packed.

exercises.name: Double Kettlebell Swing
steps: A swing with a kettlebell in each hand, feet set slightly wider.
Roughly doubles the load, so keep the reps crisp and the back flat.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Swing
steps: A hip-hinge swing holding one dumbbell vertically by the head.
The obvious swing substitute when there's no kettlebell; snap the hips and let the arms be ropes.

exercises.name: Banded Kettlebell Swing
steps: A swing with a band running from the bell to the floor for extra resistance at the top.
Forces a sharper hip snap; keep the reps low and explosive.

exercises.name: Lateral Box Jump
steps: A box jump taking off and landing sideways onto the box.
Builds lateral power most jumping never touches; land softly with the knees tracking out.

exercises.name: Single-Leg Box Jump
steps: A box jump taking off from one leg onto a low box.
Demanding on the ankle and knee -- start very low and step down between reps.

exercises.name: Vertical Jump
steps: A maximal two-foot jump straight up, reaching for a target.
The simplest measure of lower-body power; take full rest between reps.

exercises.name: Hurdle Jump
steps: Consecutive two-foot jumps over a line of low hurdles.
Trains fast, stiff ground contacts; keep the ground time short.

exercises.name: Split Jump
steps: From a lunge, jump straight up and land in the same stance without switching legs.
A single-leg power builder; keep the front knee stable on landing.

exercises.name: Countermovement Jump
steps: A vertical jump with a fast dip before takeoff.
Trains the stretch-shortening cycle; go for maximum height on every rep.

exercises.name: Seated Box Jump
steps: A box jump starting seated on a bench, so there's no countermovement to help you.
Pure concentric power; stand fully at the top of each rep.

exercises.name: Depth Drop
steps: Step off a low box and land in an athletic position, absorbing the landing softly.
Teaches the landing mechanics that make jump training safe; master this before depth jumps.

exercises.name: World's Greatest Stretch
steps: From a deep lunge, plant both hands inside your front foot.
Rotate your torso and reach that same-side arm toward the ceiling while keeping your back leg straight.
Flows through hip, hamstring, and thoracic mobility in one move.

exercises.name: Cat-Cow Stretch
steps: On hands and knees, alternate between arching your back and dropping your belly (cow) and rounding your spine toward the ceiling while tucking your chin (cat).
Move slowly with your breath to mobilize the whole spine.

exercises.name: Thoracic Spine Rotation
steps: On hands and knees or in a side-lying position, place one hand behind your head and rotate that elbow up toward the ceiling, following it with your eyes.
Isolate the rotation in your upper back rather than your hips.

exercises.name: 90/90 Hip Stretch
steps: Sit with your front leg bent 90° in front of you and your back leg bent 90° to the side, both knees on the ground.
Lean your torso forward over the front shin.
Switch sides to work internal and external hip rotation.

exercises.name: Deep Squat Hold
steps: Lower into the bottom of a bodyweight squat with your heels flat and chest up.
Hold the position for time.
Using your elbows to gently press your knees outward.
Builds ankle, hip, and lower-back mobility over time.

exercises.name: Cossack Squat
steps: From a wide stance.
Shift your weight into one bent leg while keeping the other leg straight with its foot flat, sinking as low as comfortable.
Push back to center and repeat on the other side.
A lateral squat that opens the hips and inner thighs.

exercises.name: Hip Flexor Stretch
steps: From a half-kneeling lunge position, tuck your pelvis under and gently shift your weight forward until you feel a stretch in the front of the rear hip.
Keep your torso upright rather than leaning forward to increase the range.

exercises.name: Pigeon Pose
steps: From a plank or tabletop position.
Bring one knee forward and place it behind your wrist with that shin angled across your body.
Extend the back leg straight behind you and fold forward over the front leg.
A deep hip and glute stretch.

exercises.name: Downward Dog
steps: From hands and knees.
Lift your hips up and back to form an inverted V.
Pressing your heels toward the floor and your chest toward your thighs.
Stretches the hamstrings, calves, and shoulders together.

exercises.name: Shoulder Dislocates
steps: Holding a light band or stick with a wide overhand grip.
Raise it overhead and rotate it behind your back until it reaches your glutes.
Reverse.
Keep your arms straight throughout and only go as wide as your shoulders allow without pain.

exercises.name: Arm Circles
steps: Extend your arms straight out to the sides and make small, controlled circles, gradually increasing the size.
Reverse direction.
A simple warm-up move to loosen the shoulder joint before pressing or overhead work.

exercises.name: Band Pull-Apart
steps: Hold a resistance band at chest height with arms extended.
Pull it apart by squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Keeping your arms straight the whole time.
Targets the rear delts and upper back for better shoulder posture.

exercises.name: Wall Slides
steps: Stand with your back, head, and arms pressed against a wall in a goalpost position.
Slide your arms up overhead and back down while keeping every point of contact on the wall.
Improves overhead shoulder mobility and scapular control.

exercises.name: Leg Swings
steps: Holding onto something for balance.
Swing one leg forward and back in a controlled arc.
Switch to side-to-side swings.
A dynamic hip mobility warm-up, best done before squats or running rather than as a static hold.

exercises.name: Walking Knee Hug
steps: Step forward.
Pull one knee up toward your chest with both hands and hold briefly.
Step through into the next stride and repeat on the other leg.
A dynamic hip and glute stretch that doubles as a warm-up walk.

exercises.name: Spiderman Lunge with Reach
steps: Step into a deep lunge with your hand on the ground inside your front foot.
Rotate and reach the opposite arm toward the ceiling, following it with your eyes.
Combines a hip flexor stretch with thoracic rotation.

exercises.name: Standing Quad Stretch
steps: Balancing on one leg, grab your other ankle behind you and pull your heel toward your glutes while keeping your knees close together and hips pushed slightly forward.
Hold and switch sides.

exercises.name: Ankle Mobility Drill
steps: In a half-kneeling position.
Drive your front knee forward over your toes while keeping your heel flat on the ground, repeating for reps.
Builds the ankle range of motion needed for a deeper, safer squat.

exercises.name: Scorpion Stretch
steps: Lie face down with arms out to the sides.
Lift one leg and rotate your hips to bring that foot toward the opposite hand.
Keeping your chest on the floor.
A dynamic stretch for the hips and lower back.

exercises.name: Foam Rolling
steps: Slowly roll the target muscle group over a foam roller.
Pausing on tender spots for 20-30 seconds rather than rushing across them.
Used as a warm-up or recovery tool to reduce muscle tightness before or after training.

exercises.name: Sprint Starts
steps: From a standing or three-point start, explode into a 10-20m sprint at maximum effort.
Focusing on a strong first-step drive and gradual rise out of your low body position.
Rest fully between reps since this trains raw acceleration, not endurance.

exercises.name: Flying Sprints
steps: Build up speed over 20-30m before hitting a marked "fly zone," then sprint that zone at top speed.
Trains maximum velocity mechanics rather than the acceleration phase, since you're already at speed when the timed section starts.

exercises.name: Hill Sprints
steps: Sprint uphill at maximum effort for 10-20 seconds.
Walk back down to recover fully before the next rep.
The incline forces powerful hip and knee drive while naturally limiting impact stress compared to flat-ground sprinting.

exercises.name: Resisted Sprint (Sled Push)
steps: Load a sled with a moderate weight and push it forward in short, explosive sprint bursts.
Staying low with strong leg drive.
Builds sprint-specific power without the technical demands of loaded barbell lifts.

exercises.name: Sled Drag
steps: Attach a sled to a harness or rope and drag it forward or backward for distance at a steady pace.
A joint-friendly way to build work capacity and leg drive strength with minimal eccentric muscle damage.

exercises.name: Box Jump
steps: From a quarter-squat position.
Swing your arms and jump onto a box.
Landing softly with bent knees.
Step back down (don't jump down).
Focus on landing quietly and under control rather than jumping the highest box available.

exercises.name: Depth Jump
steps: Step off a low box, land on both feet, and immediately explode into a maximal vertical jump the instant you touch the ground.
An advanced reactive-power drill; keep the ground contact time as short as possible.

exercises.name: Broad Jump
steps: From a two-foot stance.
Swing your arms back then forward and jump as far horizontally as you can.
Landing softly in a controlled squat.
Measure your distance to track progress in horizontal power output.

exercises.name: Lateral Bound
steps: Push off one leg explosively to jump sideways.
Landing softly on the opposite leg and holding the landing for a moment before repeating back the other way.
Builds the single-leg lateral power used in cutting and direction changes.

exercises.name: Single-Leg Bound
steps: Hop forward repeatedly on one leg.
Driving your opposite knee up for momentum and absorbing each landing before immediately springing into the next bound.
A demanding single-leg power and stability drill.

exercises.name: Agility Ladder Drills
steps: Run through footwork patterns (e.g. two-feet-in-each-box, lateral shuffles, in-and-outs) through a flat agility ladder on the ground.
Prioritize quick, precise foot placement over raw speed at first.
Build up pace.

exercises.name: Cone Shuttle Run
steps: Sprint between two or more cones set a fixed distance apart, decelerating and changing direction sharply at each one.
Trains the deceleration and re-acceleration mechanics that matter more in sport than straight-line speed alone.

exercises.name: 5-10-5 Pro Agility Drill
steps: Starting at a middle cone, sprint 5 yards to one side, touch the line, sprint 10 yards to the far cone, touch that line.
Sprint 5 yards back through the start.
A standard test/drill for change-of-direction speed.

exercises.name: T-Drill
steps: Sprint forward to a cone, shuffle laterally to a second cone, shuffle across to a third, shuffle back to the second.
Backpedal to the start.
A classic drill combining forward sprinting, lateral shuffling, and backpedaling.

exercises.name: Reactive Ball Drop Drill
steps: Have a partner drop a ball (or reaction ball) from shoulder height without warning while you stand ready a few feet away, and react to catch it before its second bounce.
Trains reaction time and first-step quickness.

exercises.name: Medicine Ball Rotational Throw
steps: Stand side-on to a wall, load your hips by rotating away from it.
Explosively rotate through your core and throw the medicine ball into the wall.
A rotational power move that carries over well to throwing and striking sports.

exercises.name: Medicine Ball Chest Pass
steps: Hold the medicine ball at chest height and explosively push/throw it forward into a wall or to a partner.
Catching the rebound and resetting.
Trains upper-body explosive power in a pushing pattern.

exercises.name: Medicine Ball Slam
steps: Raise the medicine ball overhead.
Explosively slam it into the ground as hard as possible by driving through your hips and core.
Catching the bounce or picking it back up to reset.
A full-body power and conditioning move.

exercises.name: Jump Rope
steps: Jump rope with small, quick hops off the balls of your feet and minimal knee bend.
Keeping the rope turn coming from your wrists rather than your whole arm.
Builds calf/ankle stiffness and rhythm useful for sprinting and change of direction.

exercises.name: High Knees
steps: Run in place (or move forward slowly) driving your knees up to hip height as quickly as possible.
Staying on the balls of your feet.
A sprint-mechanics drill for quick ground contact and knee drive.

exercises.name: Butt Kicks
steps: Jog in place or forward, kicking your heels up to touch your glutes on each stride.
A running-mechanics drill that emphasizes fast hamstring recoil, complementary to High Knees.

exercises.name: A-Skip
steps: Skip forward driving one knee up to hip height with a quick, punchy ground contact on the opposite foot, alternating sides.
A foundational sprint-drill teaching proper knee drive and posture at low speed.

exercises.name: B-Skip
steps: Same knee-drive skip as an A-Skip.
Extend the raised leg out and "claw" it back down and under your body before it lands.
Teaches the active ground-strike mechanics used in top-speed sprinting.

exercises.name: Bounding
steps: Run with exaggerated, powerful strides.
Driving off each leg to cover as much ground as possible per step and hang in the air momentarily.
A running-specific power drill that bridges jump training and sprinting.

exercises.name: Plyo Push-Up
steps: Perform a push-up explosively enough that your hands leave the ground at the top.
Landing softly with bent elbows to absorb the impact before the next rep.
Builds upper-body explosive pushing power.

exercises.name: Squat Jump
steps: From a quarter or half squat, jump straight up as high as possible and land softly back into the squat position, resetting before the next rep.
A foundational lower-body power exercise with no eccentric "catch" of a box.

exercises.name: Tuck Jump
steps: Jump straight up and pull both knees up toward your chest at the peak of the jump.
Land softly and immediately reset.
Emphasizes rapid hip flexion and reactive power in a short ground-contact time.

exercises.name: Lateral Skater Jump
steps: Push off one leg to leap sideways like a speed skater.
Landing softly on the opposite leg while the trailing leg swings behind for balance.
Immediately bound back the other way.
Builds lateral power and single-leg control together.

exercises.name: Suitcase Carry
steps: Carry a single heavy weight in one hand at your side, like a suitcase, walking tall without letting your torso lean toward the loaded side.
Trains anti-lateral-flexion core strength and real-world one-handed carrying capacity.

exercises.name: Overhead Carry
steps: Press a weight overhead and walk with it locked out above your shoulder.
Keeping your ribs down and core braced so your lower back doesn't arch.
Builds shoulder stability and overhead strength endurance together.

exercises.name: Sandbag Carry
steps: Hug or shoulder a loaded sandbag and walk for distance or time, resetting your grip/position as needed since the sand shifts unlike a fixed weight.
The shifting load adds a real-world stabilization demand machines don't replicate.

exercises.name: Sandbag Clean
steps: Hinge down to grip the sandbag.
Explosively extend your hips and pull it up to your chest/shoulder in one motion.
Using your legs and hips rather than your lower back.
Mirrors the real-world motion of picking something heavy up off the floor.

exercises.name: Sandbag Shouldering
steps: Deadlift the sandbag up to your thighs.
Use hip drive and momentum to heave it up and over onto one shoulder.
Catching it with bent knees.
A practical strength-and-power move for lifting awkward, heavy objects.

exercises.name: Zercher Carry
steps: Cradle a weight in the crooks of your elbows against your torso and walk with it.
Keeping your chest up and core tight against the front-loaded position.
Builds the upper-back and core strength needed to hold something bulky close to your body.

exercises.name: Yoke Walk
steps: Step under a loaded yoke frame resting across your upper back (like a heavy squat position).
Lift it off the rack, and walk it forward for distance.
Trains total-body loaded carrying strength under a heavier axial load than hand carries.

exercises.name: Turkish Get-Up
steps: Starting lying on your back holding a weight locked out overhead, move through a series of controlled steps.
Roll to an elbow, to a hand, bridge the hips.
Sweep the leg through.
Stand up.
All while keeping the weight overhead; go slow and light while learning the sequence.

exercises.name: Bear Crawl
steps: On hands and feet with knees hovering just off the ground, crawl forward moving opposite hand and foot together.
Keeping your hips low and back flat.
Builds full-body coordination, shoulder stability, and core control.

exercises.name: Crawling Drill
steps: Move slowly across the floor on hands and knees or hands and feet in varied patterns (forward, backward, lateral).
Keeping your core braced and movements controlled.
Used as a warm-up or restorative full-body coordination drill.

exercises.name: Sit-to-Stand
steps: From a seated position on a chair or bench.
Stand up fully without using your hands for assistance if possible.
Sit back down under control.
A direct, functional test and builder of the leg strength needed for everyday standing/sitting.

exercises.name: Floor-to-Stand Get-Up
steps: Practice getting up from lying on the floor to standing using different strategies (rolling to a kneel, half-kneeling to stand) without always using the same hand/leg.
Builds the practical strength and coordination to get up off the ground unassisted.

exercises.name: Loaded Stair Climb
steps: Carry a weighted backpack, sandbag, or dumbbells while walking up and down a flight of stairs for time or reps.
A practical way to train the leg strength and cardiovascular capacity needed for carrying loads up real stairs.

exercises.name: Tire Flip
steps: Squat down to get your hands under a large tire.
Drive through your legs and hips to flip it up and over.
Reset and repeat.
A full-body power move that mimics lifting and repositioning heavy, awkward objects.

exercises.name: Deadlift to Shoulder (Sandbag)
steps: Deadlift a sandbag off the floor.
In one continuous motion use hip drive to bring it up and rest it on one shoulder.
Combines a hip-hinge pull with a loaded carry setup, directly useful for lifting and repositioning heavy bags or people.

exercises.name: Zercher Squat
steps: Cradle the bar or weight in the crooks of your elbows in front of your chest.
Squat down and back up keeping your torso as upright as possible.
The front-loaded position builds serious core and upper-back strength alongside your legs.

exercises.name: Suitcase Deadlift
steps: Deadlift a single weight positioned at your side (like a suitcase) rather than centered.
Keeping your torso from tipping toward the load.
Trains unilateral pulling strength and anti-lateral-flexion core stability at once.

exercises.name: Single-Arm Farmer's Carry
steps: Carry a heavy weight in just one hand while walking tall and resisting the pull to lean or shrug toward that side.
A more demanding core and grip challenge than carrying weight in both hands.

exercises.name: Wheelbarrow Carry
steps: One partner holds another's ankles while the second walks forward on their hands.
A classic partner drill for shoulder stability, core control, and upper-body carrying strength; go slow on an even surface.

exercises.name: Log Press
steps: Clean a thick log implement to your chest.
Press it overhead using leg drive to help initiate the movement.
The thick, neutral grip and shifting weight distribution make this a more real-world pressing pattern than a barbell.

exercises.name: Atlas Stone Lift
steps: Hug a heavy, round stone against your body.
Lift it off the ground using your legs and hips, and load it onto a platform.
An advanced strongman movement that trains raw lifting strength for oddly-shaped, heavy objects.

exercises.name: Keg Carry
steps: Hug a loaded keg (or similarly bulky, shifting-weight object) against your chest and walk for distance.
Keeping your core braced against the awkward load.
Builds the bear-hug carrying strength useful for moving bulky household items.

exercises.name: Single-Leg Balance Hold
steps: Stand on one leg and hold your balance for time.
Keeping your standing knee soft and core engaged.
Progress by closing your eyes or standing on an unstable surface once flat-ground holds feel easy.

exercises.name: Single-Leg Romanian Deadlift
steps: Standing on one leg.
Hinge at the hips and lower a weight toward the floor while your free leg extends straight behind you for counterbalance.
Return to standing.
Trains hamstring/glute strength and balance together.

exercises.name: Bosu Ball Squat
steps: Stand on the flat or dome side of a Bosu ball and perform a bodyweight squat.
Using the instability to challenge your ankle and knee stabilizers.
Go light on load and focus on control rather than depth or speed.

exercises.name: Bosu Ball Balance Hold
steps: Stand on top of a Bosu ball (dome side down) and hold your balance, making small constant adjustments through your ankles and hips.
A foundational stability drill before adding movement on an unstable surface.

exercises.name: Single-Leg Box Step-Down
steps: Stand on a low box on one leg.
Slowly lower your other foot to lightly tap the ground before returning to standing, without letting your standing knee cave inward.
Trains eccentric single-leg control, a key piece of injury-resistant knees.

exercises.name: Tandem Stance Hold
steps: Stand with one foot directly in front of the other, heel-to-toe, and hold the position for time.
A simple, low-equipment balance drill that gets harder with eyes closed or on a softer surface.

exercises.name: Heel-to-Toe Walk
steps: Walk forward in a straight line placing the heel of one foot directly against the toes of the other with each step.
A dynamic balance drill that also doubles as a basic coordination/sobriety-style test.

exercises.name: Single-Leg Deadlift Reach
steps: Standing on one leg.
Hinge forward and reach one or both hands toward the floor while your free leg lifts straight behind you.
Return to standing.
A bodyweight balance-and-hamstring drill, a lighter regression of the loaded single-leg RDL.

exercises.name: Stability Ball Plank
steps: Hold a forearm plank with your forearms resting on a stability ball instead of the floor, bracing your core to keep the ball from rolling.
The unstable base demands more core control than a standard plank.

exercises.name: Stability Ball Hamstring Curl
steps: Lying on your back with heels on a stability ball.
Lift your hips up.
Bend your knees to roll the ball toward your glutes and back out.
Trains hamstrings and core stability against the ball's instability.

exercises.name: Single-Leg Glute Bridge
steps: Lying on your back with one foot planted and the other leg extended straight.
Drive through the planted heel to lift your hips up.
Squeezing your glute at the top.
Isolates one side at a time and exposes side-to-side strength differences.

exercises.name: Balance Beam Walk
steps: Walk heel-to-toe along a low balance beam (or a taped line on the floor as a regression).
Keeping your eyes forward rather than looking down at your feet.
Trains dynamic balance and postural control while moving.

exercises.name: Slackline Balance
steps: Stand and balance on a slackline anchored low to the ground between two points.
Using small ankle and hip adjustments to stay centered.
An advanced, highly engaging balance challenge; start near a wall or support to catch yourself.

exercises.name: Single-Leg Hop and Stick
steps: Hop forward on one leg and land softly.
Holding the landing completely still ("sticking" it) for a couple seconds before the next hop.
Trains the deceleration and landing control that protects knees during sport.

exercises.name: Wobble Board Balance
steps: Stand on a wobble board and work to keep it level and stable, making constant small corrections through your ankles.
Commonly used in ankle-injury rehab and general proprioception training.

exercises.name: Pallof Press
steps: Holding a cable or band at chest height, anchored to your side.
Press it straight out in front of you and hold.
The cable pulls you to rotate, and resisting that pull (not creating movement) is the entire point of the exercise, training anti-rotation core strength.

exercises.name: Standing Y-Balance Reach
steps: Standing on one leg.
Reach your free leg out in front, then to the side, then behind you in a Y-shaped pattern, while keeping your standing leg stable.
Switch sides.
A common screening and training drill for single-leg balance and control.

exercises.name: Prenatal Cat-Cow Stretch
steps: On hands and knees, gently arch and round your back with your breath.
Keeping the movement small and pain-free.
Relieves lower-back tension and is considered safe throughout pregnancy; stop if you feel any pulling discomfort.

exercises.name: Pelvic Tilt
steps: Standing or on hands and knees, gently tuck your pelvis under and flatten your lower back.
Release back to neutral.
Builds core awareness and can ease pregnancy-related lower-back pain; keep the motion slow and controlled.

exercises.name: Kegel Exercise
steps: Contract the pelvic floor muscles (as if stopping the flow of urine) and hold briefly before releasing, repeating for reps.
Supports pelvic floor strength during and after pregnancy; can be done seated, standing, or lying down.

exercises.name: Bird Dog
steps: On hands and knees.
Extend one arm and the opposite leg straight out while keeping your hips and shoulders level and core braced.
Return and switch sides.
Builds core stability without any spinal loading, making it a safe option through pregnancy.

exercises.name: Wall Push-Up
steps: Stand facing a wall with hands shoulder-width apart on it.
Bend your elbows to bring your chest toward the wall and press back out.
A lower-intensity, upright pushing exercise that avoids lying face-down.

exercises.name: Seated Row (Band)
steps: Sitting with legs extended and a band looped around your feet.
Pull the handles toward your torso while squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Extend back out with control.
A joint-friendly way to train the back and posture.

exercises.name: Standing Band Row
steps: Anchor a band at chest height.
Step back to create tension.
Pull the band toward your torso squeezing your shoulder blades together.
A low-impact, standing alternative to seated cable or barbell rows.

exercises.name: Side-Lying Leg Lift
steps: Lying on your side with your body in a straight line.
Lift your top leg up toward the ceiling with control.
Lower it back down without letting it rest.
Targets the hip and outer glute with no spinal loading, comfortable in most trimesters.

exercises.name: Side-Lying Clam Shell
steps: Lying on your side with knees bent and stacked.
Keep your feet together and lift your top knee open like a clamshell.
Lower with control.
A gentle, targeted hip-stability exercise commonly used in prenatal and postpartum programs.

exercises.name: Prenatal Squat (Supported)
steps: Holding onto a sturdy support (chair back, countertop, or wall) for balance, perform a shallow, controlled squat within a comfortable range.
The support reduces balance demands as your center of gravity shifts through pregnancy.

exercises.name: Chair Squat
steps: Stand in front of a sturdy chair and lower yourself down to lightly tap it before standing back up.
Using it as a depth guide and safety net.
A beginner-friendly, low-impact way to build leg strength.

exercises.name: Wall Sit (Light)
steps: Lean your back against a wall and slide down to a shallow, comfortable knee bend.
Holding the position for a short time.
A static, low-impact way to build leg endurance; keep the angle shallow and stop if you feel strain.

exercises.name: Standing Bicep Curl (Light Dumbbell)
steps: Standing with a light dumbbell in each hand.
Curl the weight up toward your shoulders keeping your elbows pinned to your sides.
Lower with control.
Light-load arm work that's safe and comfortable throughout pregnancy.

exercises.name: Seated Shoulder Press (Light)
steps: Seated with light dumbbells at shoulder height.
Press them straight overhead without arching your lower back.
Lower with control.
The seated position and light load make this a stable, joint-friendly shoulder exercise.

exercises.name: Prenatal Walking
steps: Walk at a comfortable, conversational pace for 15-30 minutes, adjusting duration and pace to how you feel that day.
One of the most recommended forms of cardio throughout pregnancy: low-impact, easy to scale, and no special equipment needed.

exercises.name: Stationary Cycling (Light)
steps: Ride a stationary bike at a light, comfortable resistance and pace.
Staying well within a conversational effort level.
The fixed, supported position makes this a stable low-impact cardio option, especially as balance shifts later in pregnancy.

exercises.name: Water Aerobics
steps: Perform gentle aerobic movements (marching, arm circles, leg swings) while standing in chest-deep water.
The water's buoyancy supports your joints and changing center of gravity while still providing resistance, making it a popular and comfortable prenatal option.

exercises.name: Prenatal Yoga Flow
steps: Move through a gentle, pregnancy-modified yoga sequence focused on breath, hip openers, and posture.
Avoids deep twists, prone (face-down) poses, and lying flat on your back for extended periods; a class or instructor-led video is recommended for proper modifications.

exercises.name: Standing Pelvic Circles
steps: Standing with feet hip-width apart and hands on your hips, slowly circle your hips in one direction and then the other.
Eases lower-back and pelvic tension and is commonly used to encourage comfortable positioning later in pregnancy.

exercises.name: Modified Side Plank (Knee Down)
steps: Lying on your side, prop up on your forearm with your bottom knee bent on the ground for support.
Lift your hips into a shortened side plank.
Trains core and hip stability with a much lower core-pressure demand than a full plank.

exercises.name: Seated Leg Extension (Light)
steps: Seated in a chair.
Extend one leg straight out in front of you and hold briefly.
Lower with control and repeat.
Adding a light ankle weight only if comfortable.
A simple, joint-friendly way to maintain quad strength.

exercises.name: Ankle Pumps
steps: Seated or lying down.
Flex your feet up and point them down in a slow, controlled pumping motion.
A gentle circulation-boosting movement often recommended during pregnancy (and after long periods of sitting) to help reduce swelling.
